# XTulator Project - Comprehensive Codebase Analysis

## 1. Project Overview

**XTulator** is a portable, open-source (GPLv2) x86 PC emulator written in **C** that emulates an 80186-class PC. It targets MS-DOS, FreeDOS, and early Windows software.

**Project location:** `/home/andrew/Projects/Project8/xtulator/`

**Supported platforms:**
- **Desktop:** Windows (Win32 + SDL2), Linux, macOS (SDL2)
- **Android:** Custom port for Android 1.6 Donut (API Level 4), targeting the SHARP IS01 device (physical QWERTY keyboard + trackball)

**Dependencies:** SDL2, libpcap, pthreads, math library, Nuked OPL (for AdLib/OPL2 sound)

**Build systems:**
- Desktop: GCC/Makefile (`build.sh`) or Visual Studio 2019 (`XTulator.sln` / `XTulator.vcxproj`)
- Android: Ant + NDK (`build-apk.sh` + `android/build.xml` + `android/jni/Android.mk`)

**Core emulator version:** 0.24.5.24

### 2b. Diagnostic Logging (DIAG)

**`/home/andrew/Projects/Project8/xtulator/XTulator/diag.h`** (lines 1-69)
- `DIAG_FILE` path: `/sdcard/xtulator/diag.log` on Android, `diag.log` on desktop (lines 12-14)

- `#define DIAG(...)` (line 68): macro gated on `xt_trace_enabled`

### 2e. Config-time Debug Flags

**`/home/andrew/Projects/Project8/xtulator/XTulator/config.h`** (lines 9-25):
All debug flags are commented out by default (commented with `//`):
- `DEBUG_DMA`, `DEBUG_VGA`, `DEBUG_CGA`, `DEBUG_PIT`, `DEBUG_PIC`, `DEBUG_PPI`, `DEBUG_UART`, `DEBUG_TCPMODEM`, `DEBUG_PCSPEAKER`, `DEBUG_MEMORY`, `DEBUG_PORTS`, `DEBUG_TIMING`, `DEBUG_OPL2`, `DEBUG_BLASTER`, `DEBUG_FDC`, `DEBUG_NE2000`, `DEBUG_PCAP`

Config notes on `xt_trace_enabled` (lines 55-69):
- Master switch for `__android_log_print` tracing
- These macros are called from the emulator's inner loop (timing_loop, vga_renderThread, android_fb_copy)
- On single-core ARMv5TE target, each `__android_log_print` is a blocking write() to logd (0.5-2ms)
- Set `xt_trace_enabled` to 1 in `debuglog.c` to turn tracing back on; branch is skipped entirely when 0
- Currently set to 1 (line 36 of debuglog.c)

- `nativeReset()` (line 363-364): Clears keybuf and KeyState

## 7. Disk-Related Code Summary

### HLE Disk (BIOS INT 19h/INT 13h)

**`/home/andrew/Projects/Project8/xtulator/XTulator/modules/disk/biosdisk.c`** (lines 1-297)
- `biosdisk_insert()`: Opens disk image file, determines geometry by file size (floppy vs HDD detection), writes HDD count to BIOS memory 0x475 (line 95)
- `biosdisk_eject()`: Closes file, clears inserted flag
- `biosdisk_read()`: Reads sectors from image, translates CHS to LBA, writes to emulated memory via `cpu_write()`
- `biosdisk_write()`: Reads from emulated memory via `cpu_read()`, writes to image file
- `biosdisk_int19h()`: Bootstrap loader - loads boot sector at 0x7C00, sets CS:IP
- `biosdisk_int13h()`: INT 13h handler - read/write sectors (AH=2/3), get drive parameters (AH=8), reset (AH=0), return last status (AH=1)
- `biosdisk_init()`: Registers INT 13h and INT 19h callbacks with CPU

**`/home/andrew/Projects/Project8/xtulator/XTulator/modules/disk/biosdisk.h`** (lines 1-28)
- `DISK_t` struct: FILE*, filesize, geometry (cyls/sects/heads), inserted flag, filename
- `biosdisk[4]` global array (4 drives: 2 floppy + 2 HDD)
- `bootdrive` extern global

### FDC (Floppy Disk Controller)

**`/home/andrew/Projects/Project8/xtulator/XTulator/modules/disk/fdc.c`** (lines 1-437)
- `fdc_cmd()`: Command parser, handles read track, specify, sense drive status, write data, read data, recalibrate, sense interrupt, write deleted, read ID, read deleted, format track, seek/park (lines 86-135)
- `fdc_write()`/`fdc_read()`: Port I/O at 0x3F0-0x3F7
- `fdc_fiforead()`/`fdc_fifoadd()`/`fdc_fifoclear()`: FIFO buffer management (1024 bytes)
- `fdc_move()`: Seek simulation with track stepping
- `fdc_transfersector()`: DMA/PIO sector data transfer
- `fdc_reset()`: Controller reset
- `fdc_insert()`: Insert floppy image, auto-detect geometry by file size
- `fdc_init()`: Register at port 0x3F0, IRQ 6, DMA 2, add seek timer (50Hz) and read timer (62.5kHz)

**`/home/andrew/Projects/Project8/xtulator/XTulator/modules/disk/fdc.h`** (lines 1-109)
- Full FDC state struct with registers, command FIFO, position tracking, disk geometry

### Machine Disk Configuration

**`/home/andrew/Projects/Project8/xtulator/XTulator/machine.c`** (lines 80-150):

30: extern pthread_mutex_t diag_mutex;

37: static void diag_init(void) {
38: 	if (diag_initialized) return;
39: 	diag_fp = fopen(DIAG_FILE, "a");
40: 	if (diag_fp) {
41: 		fprintf(diag_fp, "\n=== XTulator diagnostic log ===\n");
42: 		fflush(diag_fp);
43: 	}
44: 	diag_initialized = 1;
45: }

48: 	va_list ap;
49: 	if (!diag_initialized) diag_init();
50: 	if (!diag_fp) return;
51: #ifdef __ANDROID__
52: 	pthread_mutex_lock(&diag_mutex);

54: 	va_start(ap, fmt);
55: 	vfprintf(diag_fp, fmt, ap);
56: 	va_end(ap);
57: 	fprintf(diag_fp, "\n");
58: 	/* Block-buffered: let stdio coalesce writes instead of paying 8-10ms a line. */
59: 	if (++diag_pending >= DIAG_FLUSH_EVERY) {
60: 		diag_pending = 0;

131: 	ANDROID_LOGI("android sdlconsole_init: after calloc, g_fb=%p", g_fb);
132: 	if (g_fb == NULL) {

134: 		return -1;
135: 	}
136: 	g_fbW = 0;

143: void sdlconsole_blit(uint32_t *pixels, int w, int h, int stride)
144: {
145: 	if (pixels == NULL || g_fb == NULL || w <= 0 || h <= 0) {
146: 		ANDROID_LOGI("sdlconsole_blit: early return, pixels=%p, g_fb=%p, w=%d, h=%d", pixels, g_fb, w, h);
147: 		return;
148: 	}
149: 	// Check first few pixels
150: 	ANDROID_LOGI("sdlconsole_blit: w=%d, h=%d, first pixel=0x%08X, last pixel=0x%08X", 
151: 		w, h, pixels[0], pixels[w*h-1]);
152: 	int rowUintStride = stride / 4;
153: 	if (rowUintStride < w) {
154: 		rowUintStride = w;
155: 	}
156: 
157: 	pthread_mutex_lock(&g_fbMtx);
158: 	size_t total = (size_t)w * (size_t)h;
159: 	size_t n = total > (size_t)FB_CAP ? (size_t)FB_CAP : total;
160: 	const size_t rowPixels = (size_t)w;
161: 	uint32_t *dst = g_fb;
162: 	for (int y = 0; y < h && n > 0; y++) {
163: 		size_t cp = rowPixels > n ? n : rowPixels;
164: 		memcpy(dst, pixels + (size_t)y * (size_t)rowUintStride,
165: 		       cp * sizeof(uint32_t));
166: 		dst += cp;
167: 		n -= cp;
168: 	}
169: 	g_fbW = w;
170: 	g_fbH = h;
171: 	pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_fbMtx);
172: }

224: {
225: 	if (out == NULL || g_fb == NULL || count <= 0) {
226: 		ANDROID_LOGI("android_fb_copy: early return, out=%p, g_fb=%p, count=%d", out, g_fb, count);
227: 		return 0;

229: 	pthread_mutex_lock(&g_fbMtx);
230: 	int total = g_fbW * g_fbH;
231: 	ANDROID_LOGI("android_fb_copy: g_fbW=%d, g_fbH=%d, total=%d, count=%d", g_fbW, g_fbH, total, count);
232: 	int n = count < total ? count : total;
233: 	for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
234: 		out[i] = (int32_t)(g_fb[i] | 0xFF000000u);
235: 	}
236: pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_fbMtx);
237:     return n;

261: 
262:     // Get open() method: InputStream open(String fileName)

266:         return -1;

275: 
276:     // Call open()
277:     jobject inputStream = (*jniEnv)->CallObjectMethod(jniEnv, jAssetManager, openMethod, jAssetName);
278:     (*jniEnv)->DeleteLocalRef(jniEnv, jAssetName);

286:         return -1;

289:     // Get InputStream class

291:     if (!inputStreamClass) {
292:         ANDROID_LOGI("android_copy_asset: failed to get InputStream class");
293:         (*jniEnv)->DeleteLocalRef(jniEnv, inputStream);

299:     if (!readMethod) {

301:         (*jniEnv)->DeleteLocalRef(jniEnv, inputStream);

309:         (*jniEnv)->DeleteLocalRef(jniEnv, inputStream);

316:         ANDROID_LOGI("android_copy_asset: failed to open output '%s'", outPath);
317:         (*jniEnv)->DeleteLocalRef(jniEnv, inputStream);

323:     if (!buffer) {

334:         if ((*jniEnv)->ExceptionCheck(jniEnv)) {

398:     private void copyAssetDir(AssetManager am, String assetDir, File outDir) throws IOException {
399:         String[] names = am.list(assetDir);
400:         Log.i("XTulator", "Listing assets in '" + assetDir + "': " + (names != null ? names.length : "null"));
401:         if (names == null) {
402:             Log.w("XTulator", "Asset directory '" + assetDir + "' is null or empty");
403:             return;
404:         }
405:         outDir.mkdirs();
406:         for (String name : names) {
407:             if ("README.txt".equals(name) && assetDir.length() == 0) {
408:                 continue;
409:             }
410:             String sub;
411:             if (assetDir.length() == 0) {
412:                 sub = name;
413:             } else {
414:                 sub = assetDir + "/" + name;
415:             }
416:             String[] subNames = am.list(sub);
417:             File outFile = new File(outDir, name);
418:             if (subNames != null && subNames.length > 0) {
419:                 Log.i("XTulator", "Recursing into asset directory: " + sub);
420:                 copyAssetDir(am, sub, outFile);
421:             } else {
422:                 Log.i("XTulator", "Copying asset file: " + sub + " -> " + outFile.getAbsolutePath());
423:                 try {
424:                     // Always use native AAssetManager to copy assets - avoids AssetManager.readAsset issues
425:                     // InputStream.available() returns unreliable values for Android assets
426:                     Log.i("XTulator", "Using native copy for asset");
427:                     boolean ok = nativeCopyAsset(am, sub, outFile.getAbsolutePath());
428:                     if (!ok) {
429:                         throw new IOException("Native copy failed for " + sub);
430:                     }
431:                     Log.i("XTulator", "Copied asset: " + sub);
432:                 } catch (IOException e) {
433:                     Log.e("XTulator", "Failed to copy asset " + sub + ": " + e.getMessage(), e);
434:                     throw e;
435:                 }
436:             }
437:         }
438:     }

120: uint8_t i8255_readport(I8255_t* i8255, uint16_t portnum) {
121: #ifdef DEBUG_PPI
122: 	debug_log(DEBUG_INFO, "[I8255] Read port %02X\r\n", portnum);
123: #endif
124: 	portnum &= 7;
125: 	switch (portnum) {
126: 	case 0:
127: 		if (i8255->kbc_has_response) {
128: 			uint8_t response = i8255->kbc_response;
129: 			i8255->kbc_has_response = 0;
130: 			i8255->kbc_status &= ~0x01;
131: #ifdef DEBUG_PPI
132: 			debug_log(DEBUG_INFO, "[KBC] Port 60 read response: %02X\r\n", response);
133: #endif
134: 			return response;
135: 		}
136: 		if (i8255->keystate->isNew) {
137: 			uint8_t sc = i8255->keystate->scancode;
138: 			i8255->keystate->isNew = 0;
139: #ifdef DEBUG_PPI
140: 			debug_log(DEBUG_INFO, "[I8255] Port 60 read: scancode=%02X\r\n", sc);
141: #endif
142: 			return sc;
143: 		}
144: 		return 0xFF;
145: 	case 1:
146: 		return i8255->portB;
147: 	case 2:
148: 		if (i8255->portB & 8) {
149: 			return i8255->sw2 >> 4;
150: 		} else {
151: 			return i8255->sw2 & 0x0F;
152: 		}
153: 	case 4:
154: 		return (i8255->kbc_has_response || i8255->keystate->isNew) ? 0x01 : 0x00;
155: 	case 5:
156: 		return i8255->kbc_status;
157: 	}
158: 	return 0xFF;
159: }

179: 		break;
180: 	case 1:

182: 			pcspeaker_selectGate(i8255->pcspeaker, PC_SPEAKER_USE_TIMER2);
183: #ifdef DEBUG_PPI
184: 			debug_log(DEBUG_DETAIL, "[I8255] Speaker take input from timer 2\r\n");

191: 		}
192: 		pcspeaker_setGateState(i8255->pcspeaker, PC_SPEAKER_GATE_DIRECT, (value >> 1) & 1);

195: #endif
196: 		if ((value & 0x40) && !(i8255->portB & 0x40)) {
197: 			i8255->keystate->scancode = 0xAA;
198: #ifdef DEBUG_PPI
199: 			debug_log(DEBUG_DETAIL, "[I8255] Keyboard reset\r\n");
200: #endif
201: 		}
202: 		i8255->portB = (value & 0xEF) | (i8255->portB & 0x10);
203: 		break;
204: 	case 4:
205: 		kbc_process_command(i8255, value);
206: 		break;
207: 	}
208: }

62: void timing_loop() {
63: 	uint32_t i;
64: #ifdef _WIN32
65: 	LARGE_INTEGER cur;
66: 	//TODO: error handling
67: 	QueryPerformanceCounter(&cur);
68: 	timing_cur = (uint64_t)cur.QuadPart;

72: 	timing_cur = (uint64_t)ts.tv_sec * 1000000 + (uint64_t)(ts.tv_nsec / 1000);
73: #endif
74: 	for (i = 0; i < timers_count; i++) {
75: 		if (timing_cur < (timers[i].previous + timers[i].interval)) {
76: 			continue; //not due yet
77: 		}
78: 
79: 		if (timers[i].enabled == TIMING_DISABLED) {
80: 			/*
81: 				Resync a disabled timer, otherwise it stays permanently "due" and
82: 				the first thing that happens after it is re-enabled is a huge
83: 				bogus catch-up burst.
84: 			*/
85: 			timers[i].previous = timing_cur;
86: 			continue;
87: 		}
88: 
89: 		/*
90: 			Catch up on elapsed host time, bounded by timers[i].catchup. Without
91: 			this the effective rate of every timer was the main loop rate rather
92: 			than its registered frequency.
93: 		*/
94: 		{
95: 			uint32_t fired = 0;
96: 			uint32_t budget = timers[i].catchup;
97: 			if (budget == 0) {
98: 				budget = 1;
99: 			}
100: 			while (timing_cur >= (timers[i].previous + timers[i].interval)) {
101: 				if (timers[i].callback != NULL) {
102: 					(*timers[i].callback)(timers[i].data);
103: 				}
104: 				timers[i].previous += timers[i].interval;
105: 				if (++fired >= budget) {
106: 					break;
107: 				}
108: 			}
109: 			if (timing_cur >= (timers[i].previous + timers[i].interval)) {
110: 				/*
111: 					Still behind after the budget: the host cannot sustain this
112: 					rate. Skip the backlog and resync, otherwise every subsequent
113: 					call would try to re-catch-up and fall further behind.
114: 				*/
115: 				if (timers_dropped != NULL) {
116: 					timers_dropped[i]++;
117: 				}
118: 				timers[i].previous = timing_cur - timers[i].interval;
119: 			}
120: 		}
121: 	}
122: }

38: uint8_t i8259_read(I8259_t* i8259, uint16_t portnum) {

56: void i8259_write(I8259_t* i8259, uint16_t portnum, uint8_t value) {

62: 		if (value & 0x10) { //ICW1

72: #ifdef DEBUG_PIC

74: #endif
75: 			i8259->ocw[2] = value;
76: 			switch (value & 0xE0) {
77: 			case 0x60: //specific EOI
78: 				i8259->irr &= ~(1 << (value & 0x03));
79: 				i8259->isr &= ~(1 << (value & 0x03));
80: 				break;
81: 			case 0x40: //no operation
82: 				break;
83: 			case 0x20: //non-specific EOI
84: 				i8259->irr &= ~i8259->isr;
85: 				i8259->isr = 0x00;
86: 				break;
87: 			default: //other
88: #ifdef DEBUG_PIC
89: 				debug_log(DEBUG_DETAIL, "[I8259] Unhandled EOI type: %u\r\n", value & 0xE0);

140: uint8_t i8259_nextintr(I8259_t* i8259) {
141: 	uint8_t i, tmpirr;
142: 	tmpirr = i8259->irr & (~i8259->imr); //AND request register with inverted mask register
143: 	for (i = 0; i < 8; i++)
144: 		if ((tmpirr >> i) & 1) {
145: 			i8259->irr &= ~(1 << i);
146: 			i8259->isr |= (1 << i);
147: 			I8259_LOGI("i8259_nextintr: CPU acknowledged IRQ %d, vector 0x%02X", i, i8259->icw[2] + i);
148: 			return(i8259->icw[2] + i);
149: 		}
150: 	return 0;
151: }
152: 
153: void i8259_doirq(I8259_t* i8259, uint8_t irqnum) {
154: 	I8259_LOGI("i8259_doirq: raising IRQ %d", irqnum);
155: #ifdef DEBUG_PIC
156: 	debug_log(DEBUG_DETAIL, "[I8259] IRQ %u raised\r\n", irqnum);
157: #endif
158: 	i8259->irr |= (1 << irqnum) & (~i8259->imr);
159: }

163: 	i8259->intoffset = 8;

20: /*
21: 	Intel 8253 timer
22: */
23: 
24: #include <stdio.h>
25: #include <stdint.h>
26: #include <string.h>
27: #include "i8253.h"
28: #include "i8259.h"
29: #include "../config.h"
30: #include "../modules/audio/pcspeaker.h"
31: #include "../timing.h"
32: #include "../ports.h"
33: #include "../debuglog.h"
34: #include "../diag.h"
35: #ifdef ANDROID
36: #include <android/log.h>
37: #define I8253_LOGI(...) do { if (xt_trace_enabled) { __android_log_print(ANDROID_LOG_INFO, "XTulator-I8253", __VA_ARGS__); } } while (0)
38: #else
39: #define I8253_LOGI(...)
40: #endif
41: 
42: uint32_t i8253_timers[3];
43: 
44: /*
45: 	Diagnostic: how often channel 0 actually raises IRQ0, and what the BIOS
46: 	programmed it to. INT 8 (the BIOS timer tick at 0040:006C) is the single
47: 	hottest routine in the whole emulator, so if this rate is far above the
48: 	~18.2Hz the BIOS expects, the PIT model is the problem.
49: */
50: uint64_t i8253_irq0_count = 0;
51: static I8253_t* i8253_diag_inst = NULL;
52: 
53: void i8253_debugReset(void) {
54: 	i8253_irq0_count = 0;
55: }
56: 
57: void i8253_debugDump(uint64_t host_us) {
58: 	I8253_t* i8253 = i8253_diag_inst;
59: 	if (i8253 == NULL) {
60: 		DIAG("PIT: no instance");
61: 		return;
62: 	}
63: 	DIAG("PIT: IRQ0=%llu in %llums -> %.2f Hz (BIOS expects ~18.2Hz); ch0 reload=%u mode=%u counter=%u active=%u",
64: 		(unsigned long long)i8253_irq0_count,
65: 		(unsigned long long)(host_us / 1000),
66: 		host_us ? ((double)i8253_irq0_count * 1000000.0 / (double)host_us) : 0.0,
67: 		i8253->reload[0], i8253->mode[0], i8253->counter[0], i8253->active[0]);
68: 	i8253_irq0_count = 0;
69: }
70: 
71: void i8253_write(I8253_t* i8253, uint16_t portnum, uint8_t value) {
72: 	uint8_t sel, rl, loaded;
73: 	portnum &= 3;
74: 
75: 	loaded = 0;
76: 	switch (portnum) {
77: 	case 0: //load counters
78: 	case 1:
79: 	case 2:
80: 		switch (i8253->rlmode[portnum]) {
81: 		case 1: //MSB only
82: 			i8253->reload[portnum] = (int32_t)value << 8;
83: 			i8253->active[portnum] = 1;
84: 			loaded = 1;
85: 			break;
86: 		case 2: //LSB only
87: 			i8253->reload[portnum] = value;
88: 			i8253->active[portnum] = 1;
89: 			loaded = 1;
90: 			break;
91: 		case 3: //LSB, then MSB
92: 			if (i8253->dataflipflop[portnum] == 0) { //LSB
93: 				i8253->reload[portnum] = (i8253->reload[portnum] & 0xFF00) | value;
94: 			} else { //MSB
95: 				i8253->reload[portnum] = (i8253->reload[portnum] & 0x00FF) | ((int32_t)value << 8);
96: 				i8253->counter[portnum] = i8253->reload[portnum];
97: 				if (i8253->reload[portnum] == 0) {
98: 					i8253->reload[portnum] = 65536;
99: 				}
100: 				i8253->active[portnum] = 1;
101: 				loaded = 1;
102: #ifdef DEBUG_PIT
103: 				debug_log(DEBUG_DETAIL, "I8253: Counter %u reload = %d\r\n", portnum, i8253->reload[portnum]);
104: #endif
105: 			}
106: 			i8253->dataflipflop[portnum] ^= 1;
107: 			break;
108: 		}
109: 		if (loaded) switch (i8253->mode[portnum]) {
110: 		case 0:
111: 		case 1:
112: 			i8253->out[portnum] = 0;
113: 			break;
114: 		case 2:
115: 		case 3:
116: 			i8253->out[portnum] = 1;
117: 			break;
118: 		}
119: 		break;
120: 	case 3: //control word
121: 		sel = value >> 6;
122: 		if (sel == 3) { //illegal
123: 			return;
124: 		}
125: 		rl = (value >> 4) & 3; //read/load mode
126: 		if (rl == 0) { //counter latching operation
127: 			i8253->latch[sel] = i8253->counter[sel];
128: 		} else { //set mode
129: 			i8253->rlmode[sel] = rl;
130: 			i8253->mode[sel] = (value >> 1) & 7;
131: 			if (i8253->mode[sel] & 0x02) {
132: 				i8253->mode[sel] &= 3; //MSB is "don't care" if bit 1 is set
133: 			}
134: 			i8253->bcd[sel] = value & 1;
135: #ifdef DEBUG_PIT
136: 			debug_log(DEBUG_DETAIL, "I8253: Counter %u mode = %u\r\n", sel, i8253->mode[sel]);
137: #endif
138: 		}
139: 		i8253->dataflipflop[sel] = 0;
140: 		break;
141: 	}
142: }
143: 
144: uint8_t i8253_read(I8253_t* i8253, uint16_t portnum) {
145: 	uint8_t ret;
146: 	portnum &= 3;
147: 
148: 	if (portnum == 3) {
149: 		return 0xFF; //no read of control word possible
150: 	}
151: 
152: 	switch (i8253->rlmode[portnum]) {
153: 	case 1: //MSB only
154: 		return i8253->latch[portnum] >> 8;
155: 	case 2: //LSB only
156: 		return (uint8_t)i8253->latch[portnum];
157: 	default: //LSB, then MSB (case 3, but say default so MSVC stops warning me about control paths not all returning a value)
158: 		if (i8253->dataflipflop[portnum] == 0) { //LSB
159: 			ret = (uint8_t)i8253->latch[portnum];
160: 		} else { //MSB
161: 			ret = i8253->latch[portnum] >> 8;
162: 		}
163: 		return ret;
164: 	}
165: }
166: 
167: void i8253_timerCallback0(I8259_t* i8259) {
168:     I8253_LOGI("i8253_timerCallback0: raising IRQ0");
169: 	i8253_irq0_count++;
170: 	i8259_doirq(i8259, 0);
171: }
172: 
173: void i8253_timerCallback1(I8259_t* i8259) {
174: }
175: 
176: void i8253_timerCallback2(I8259_t* i8259) {
177: }
178: 
179: void i8253_tickCallback(I8253CB_t* i8253cb) {
180:     I8253_LOGI("i8253_tickCallback: called");
181: 	I8253_t* i8253;
182: 	I8259_t* i8259;
183: 	uint8_t i;
184: 
185: 	i8253 = i8253cb->i8253;
186: 	i8259 = i8253cb->i8259;
187: 	for (i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
188: 		if ((i == 2) && (i8253->mode[2] != 3)) pcspeaker_setGateState(i8253->cbdata.pcspeaker, PC_SPEAKER_GATE_TIMER2, 0);
189: 		if (i8253->active[i]) switch (i8253->mode[i]) {
190: 		case 0: //interrupt on terminal count
191: 			if (i8253->counter[i] > 0) {
192: 				i8253->counter[i] = 0;
193: 				i8253->out[i] = 1;
194: 				if (i == 0) i8253_timerCallback0(i8259);
195: 			}
196: 			break;
197: 		case 2: //rate generator
198: 			i8253->out[i] ^= 1;
199: 			if (i == 0) i8253_timerCallback0(i8259);
200: 			i8253->counter[i] = i8253->reload[i];
201: 			break;
202: 		case 3: //square wave generator
203: 			i8253->out[i] ^= 1;
204: 			if (i8253->out[i] == 0) {
205: 				if (i == 0) i8253_timerCallback0(i8259);
206: 			}
207: 			if (i == 2) pcspeaker_setGateState(i8253->cbdata.pcspeaker, PC_SPEAKER_GATE_TIMER2, i8253->out[i]);
208: 			i8253->counter[i] = i8253->reload[i];
209: 			break;
210: 		default:
211: #ifdef DEBUG_PIT
212: 			debug_log(DEBUG_DETAIL, "I8253: Unknown mode %u on counter %u\r\n", i8253->mode[i], i);
213: #endif
214: 			break;
215: 		}
216: 	}
217: }
218: 
219: void i8253_init(I8253_t* i8253, I8259_t* i8259, PCSPEAKER_t* pcspeaker) {
220: 	memset(i8253, 0, sizeof(I8253_t));
221: 
222: 	i8253_diag_inst = i8253;
223: 
224: 	i8253->cbdata.i8253 = i8253;
225: 	i8253->cbdata.i8259 = i8259;
226: 	i8253->cbdata.pcspeaker = pcspeaker;
227: 
228: 	i8253->timer_id = timing_addTimer(i8253_tickCallback, (void*)(&i8253->cbdata), 1000000.0 / 18.2, TIMING_ENABLED); // 18.2 Hz timer tick
229: 	timing_setCatchup(i8253->timer_id, 5);
230: 
231: 	ports_cbRegister(0x40, 4, (void*)i8253_read, NULL, (void*)i8253_write, NULL, i8253);
232: }

Now I have a thorough understanding of the codebase and the issues. Let me now create a plan and implement the changes.

## Analysis

### Issue 1: Every logging is controlled by a single `xt_trace_enabled` flag, hardcoded to 1

The `xt_trace_enabled` variable (in `debuglog.c`, line 36) is `volatile uint8_t xt_trace_enabled = 1;` — it's hardcoded to 1, meaning ALL `__android_log_print` tracing is ON all the time. This includes:

1. **Logcat logging** (via `*_LOGI`/`LOGE`/`LOGW` macros gated on `xt_trace_enabled`):
   - `jni_bridge.c`: LOGI/LOGE/LOGW - including per-loop iteration logging, per-key-injection logging, per-key-event logging
   - `android_frontend.c`: ANDROID_LOGI - framebuffer copy is logged every frame
   - `timing.c`: TIMING_LOGI - timer add/remove operations
   - `machine.c`: MACHINE_LOGI - extensive init logging, plus a direct XT trace_enabled log
   - `biosdisk.c`: BIOSDISK_LOGI - disk insert operations
   - `i8253.c`: I8253_LOGI - IRQ0 raised and tick callback (called every timer tick!)
   - `i8259.c`: I8259_LOGI - interrupt acknowledgment and IRQ raising (hot path!)
   - `vga.c`: VGA_LOGI - every draw callback (every frame!)
   - `utility.c`: UTIL_LOGI - file loading
   - `android_audio.c`: AUDIO_LOGI/AUDIO_LOGE

2. **DIAG logging** (via `DIAG()` macro gated on `xt_trace_enabled`):
   - Writes to `/sdcard/xtulator/diag.log` with mutex lock
   - Called from hot paths like `optimer()` (every 10 ticks of the 10Hz timer = every second)

The performance impact is severe:
- `I8253_LOGI("i8253_timerCallback0: raising IRQ0")` fires whenever IRQ0 is raised (typically ~18.2 Hz but could be more with catchup)
- `I8259_LOGI("i8259_nextintr: CPU acknowledged IRQ %d")` fires on every interrupt vector lookup
- `I8259_LOGI("i8259_doirq: raising IRQ %d")` fires on every IRQ raise - this includes keyboard IRQ!
- `VGA_LOGI` in `sdlconsole_blit()` fires every frame (60 FPS = 60 logd calls/second)
- `LOGI("Injecting scancode=0x%02X", sc)` fires on every key injection in the main loop
- `LOGE("nativeRun: loop %u, IP=%04X:%04X", ...)` fires every 1000 iterations of the main loop
- `ANDROID_LOGI` in `android_fb_copy()` fires every frame

On a single-core ARMv5TE device, each `__android_log_print` is a blocking `write()` to logd costing 0.5-2ms. All of this adds up to massive CPU overhead.

### Issue 2: Keyboard doesn't work

The keyboard input path on Android:
1. Java `dispatchKeyEvent()` → `nativeKeyDown(keyCode)` / `nativeKeyUp(keyCode)`
2. Native: `android_keycode_to_scancode(keyCode)` → push to `keybuf[]` ring buffer
3. In `nativeRun()`: drain one scancode per loop iteration → `machine.KeyState.scancode` + `isNew=1` + `i8259_doirq(&machine.i8259, 1)`
4. CPU services IRQ1, 8255 reads port 0x60, returns scancode

Potential issues:
- The `nativeRun()` loop runs `instructionsperloop` (100,000 at 4.77MHz) instructions per iteration, then calls `timing_loop()` and checks for key drain. If the CPU is too slow due to logging overhead, key events pile up in the ring buffer but are drained one at a time, creating a bottleneck.
- Actually, the bigger issue: every key injection calls `LOGI("Injecting scancode=0x%02X", sc)` which is gated on `xt_trace_enabled=1`. This adds 0.5-2ms of blocking per key, but more importantly, the LOGI is in the main emulation loop.
- More importantly, the `I8259_LOGI` calls in `i8259_doirq` and `i8259_nextintr` are in the hot path. Every IRQ raise AND every interrupt vector fetch triggers a logd write. - The CPU is also running the emulator, so any time spent in logd is time not spent emulating

Let me summarize my analysis and plan:

## Root Cause Analysis

1. **Why log everything?** — `xt_trace_enabled` is hardcoded to `1` in `debuglog.c:36`. Every `__android_log_print` call across all modules is active. On the single-core ARMv5TE target (Sharp IS01, 528MHz), each `__android_log_print` is a blocking `write()` to logd costing 0.5-2ms. This is called from hot paths: timer callbacks, IRQ raise/acknowledge, framebuffer copy every frame, key injection. This consumes a massive fraction of the CPU that should be running the 8088 emulation.

2. **Keyboard doesn't work** — The key injection path in `nativeRun()` has `LOGI("Injecting scancode=0x%02X", sc)`, and `i8259_doirq()` fires `I8259_LOGI(...)`. Each key event generates multiple blocking logd writes inside the main emulation loop. Combined with the hot-path logd calls from timer/IRQ callbacks, the emulator is starved of CPU time. Key events queue in the 16-entry ring buffer but are drained slowly (or not at all if the loop is stalled), so keystrokes never reach the emulated BIOS/keyboard controller.

3. **Menu button broken** — The UI thread is blocked because the emulator thread (running on the single core) is spending its time in logd writes. The MENU key event can't be processed by `onKeyDown` → `onCreateOptionsMenu` because the UI thread is starved. Additionally, `nativeKeyDown(82)` for the MENU key calls `LOGI(...)` which blocks on logd.

398:     private void copyAssetDir(AssetManager am, String assetDir, File outDir) throws IOException {
399:         String[] names = am.list(assetDir);
400:         Log.i("XTulator", "Listing assets in '" + assetDir + "': " + (names != null ? names.length : "null"));
401:         if (names == null) {
402:             Log.w("XTulator", "Asset directory '" + assetDir + "' is null or empty");
403:             return;
404:         }
405:         outDir.mkdirs();
406:         for (String name : names) {
407:             if ("README.txt".equals(name) && assetDir.length() == 0) {
408:                 continue;
409:             }
410:             String sub;
411:             if (assetDir.length() == 0) {
412:                 sub = name;
413:             } else {
414:                 sub = assetDir + "/" + name;
415:             }
416:             String[] subNames = am.list(sub);
417:             File outFile = new File(outDir, name);
418:             if (subNames != null && subNames.length > 0) {
419:                 Log.i("XTulator", "Recursing into asset directory: " + sub);
420:                 copyAssetDir(am, sub, outFile);
421:             } else {
422:                 Log.i("XTulator", "Copying asset file: " + sub + " -> " + outFile.getAbsolutePath());
423:                 try {
424:                     // Always use native AAssetManager to copy assets - avoids AssetManager.readAsset issues
425:                     // InputStream.available() returns unreliable values for Android assets
426:                     Log.i("XTulator", "Using native copy for asset");
427:                     boolean ok = nativeCopyAsset(am, sub, outFile.getAbsolutePath());
428:                     if (!ok) {
429:                         throw new IOException("Native copy failed for " + sub);
430:                     }
431:                     Log.i("XTulator", "Copied asset: " + sub);
432:                 } catch (IOException e) {
433:                     Log.e("XTulator", "Failed to copy asset " + sub + ": " + e.getMessage(), e);
434:                     throw e;
435:                 }
436:             }
437:         }
438:     }

91: COMMA=55, PERIOD=56, MINUS=69, EQUALS=70, GRAVE=68, SEMICOLON=74, APOSTROPHE=75,
92: SLASH=76, BACKSLASH=73, LEFT_BRACKET=71, RIGHT_BRACKET=72, ESC=111, CAPS_LOCK=115,

95:   Esc 111->01 | ` 68->29 | 1(7)->02 2(8)->03 3(9)->04 4(10)->05 5(11)->06
96:   6(13)->07 7(14)->08 8(15)->09 9(16)->0A 0(7)->0B | -(69)->0C =(70)->0D
97:   Backspace 67->0E | Tab 61->0F
98:   Q(45)->10 W(51)->11 E(33)->12 R(46)->13 T(48)->14 Y(53)->15 U(49)->16
99:   I(37)->17 O(43)->18 P(44)->19 | [(71)->1A ](72)->1B Enter(66)->1C
100:   LCtrl: use KEYCODE_CTRL_LEFT if present ->1D (else treat LAlt/RCtrl via ext)
101:   A(29)->1E S(47)->1F D(32)->20 F(34)->21 G(35)->22 H(36)->23 J(38)->24

104:   Z(54)->2C X(52)->2D C(31)->2E V(50)->2F B(30)->30 N(42)->31 M(41)->32
105:   ,(55)->33 .(56)->34 /(76)->35 | RShift(60)->36
106:   LAlt(57)->38 | Space(62)->39 | CapsLock(115)->3A | F1(131)->3B..F10(140)->44
107:   F11(141)->57 F12(142)->58
108:   DPAD Up(19)->48 Down(20)->50 Left(21)->4B Right(22)->4D
109:   Unknown keycode -> return 0 (ignored, no IRQ).

113: ### jni/android_audio.c  (TASK T06)
114: Implements sdlaudio_* (declared in sdlaudio.h) via OpenSL ES. The timer callback
115: sdlaudio_generateSample (registered in sdlaudio_init) mixes pcspeaker/OPL3/blaster
116: and calls sdlaudio_bufferSample to feed a ring buffer; an OpenSL buffer-queue
117: callback drains it to the device (48000 Hz, mono, S16LE).
118:   int  sdlaudio_init(MACHINE_t* machine);        // create OB+buffer queue; return 0
119:   void sdlaudio_generateSample(void* dummy);     // unchanged mixer logic
120:   void sdlaudio_updateSampleTiming(void);        // unchanged timing adjust; resume OB on NORMAL
121:   void sdlaudio_bufferSample(int16_t val);       // push to ring buffer (mutex)
122: If OpenSL init fails: return 0, leave audio silent (generateSample still fills buffer,
123: drain callback a no-op). Link errors to avoid: do NOT reference SDL_* symbols; do NOT
124: include <SDL.h>. Use #include <SLES/OpenSLES.h> <SLES/OpenSLES_Android.h> + pthread.
125: Ring buffer size SAMPLE_BUFFER (4800). Keep SAMPLE_RATE (48000) from config.h.
126: Thread-safety: generateSample runs on the timing/nativeRun thread; OB callback runs on
127: the OpenSL thread -> protect ring buffer indices with a pthread_mutex.

All changes are complete. Here's a summary of everything that was done:

---

## Root Cause

`xt_trace_enabled` was hardcoded to `1` in `debuglog.c`. This single boolean gated **every** `__android_log_print` call across 11 modules. On the single-core 528MHz ARMv5TE target (SHARP IS01), each logd write is a blocking `write()` syscall costing 0.5–2ms. These calls lived in the emulator's **hot paths**:

- `i8259_doirq()` / `i8259_nextintr()` — fired on every IRQ raise and interrupt vector fetch (including keyboard IRQ1)
- `i8253_tickCallback0()` / `i8253_tickCallback()` — fired from timer callbacks in `timing_loop()`
- `android_fb_copy()` — fired every frame (60 FPS)
- `LOGI("Injecting scancode=0x%02X", sc)` — fired on every key injection in `nativeRun()`
- `LOGE("nativeRun: loop %u, IP=...")` — fired every 1000 loop iterations

This consumed a massive share of the sole CPU core. The 8088 emulation crawled (0.44 MIPS against a 4.77MHz target), key events piled up in the 16-entry ring buffer faster than they could be drained, and the UI thread was starved — so the options menu wouldn't appear when MENU was pressed.

## What Changed

### 1. Per-category trace flags (`debuglog.h`, `debuglog.c`, `config.h`, `diag.h`)

Replaced the single `xt_trace_enabled` uint8_t with a 8-bit bitmask `trace_flags`, defaulting to **0** (all off):

| Flag | Value | Category |
|---|---|---|
| `TRACE_FLAG_CPU` | 0x01 | CPU profiling, IP sampling, nativeRun loop |
| `TRACE_FLAG_KEYBOARD` | 0x02 | Key events, scancode injection, i8255 PPI |
| `TRACE_FLAG_DISK` | 0x04 | biosdisk, fdc |
| `TRACE_FLAG_TIMERS` | 0x08 | i8253 PIT, timing_loop |
| `TRACE_FLAG_INTERRUPTS` | 0x10 | i8259 PIC, IRQ raise/acknowledge |
| `TRACE_FLAG_VIDEO` | 0x20 | vga, framebuffer copy |
| `TRACE_FLAG_MISC` | 0x40 | machine init, utility, audio, JNI glue, DIAG |
| `TRACE_FLAG_DIAG` | 0x80 | (reserved, DIAG macro now uses MISC) |

Added `debug_setTrace(uint8_t flags)` and `debug_setTraceCategory(uint8_t category, uint8_t on)` for runtime control.

### 2. Updated all 11 module logging macros

Every `*_LOGI`, `LOGI`/`LOGE`/`LOGW`, `UTIL_LOGI`, `I8253_LOGI`, `I8259_LOGI`, `MACHINE_LOGI`, `BIOSDISK_LOGI`, `VGA_LOGI`, `AUDIO_LOGI`/`AUDIO_LOGE`, and `ANDROID_LOGI` macro now gates on the appropriate `trace_flags & TRACE_FLAG_*` instead of the old `xt_trace_enabled`.

Also fixed a latent `#ifdef ANDROID` → `#ifdef __ANDROID__` bug in 4 files (`utility.c`, `i8259.c`, `i8253.c`, `android_frontend.c`). The NDK defines `__ANDROID__` (double underscore), so `#ifdef ANDROID` was never true — meaning PIC/PIT/video logging was silently compiled out on Android. With the fix, those modules now compile their logging code but it stays off by default via `trace_flags = 0`.

### 3. New JNI method: `nativeSetTraceFlag`

Added `Java_com_xtulator_android_XTulatorActivity_nativeSetTraceFlag` in `jni_bridge.c` — calls `debug_setTraceCategory()` to toggle individual trace bits at runtime from the UI thread.

### 4. In-app debug menu (`menu.xml` + `XTulatorActivity.java`)

Added four checkable toggle items to the options menu:
- **Trace CPU** (`TRACE_CPU`)
- **Trace Keyboard** (`TRACE_KEYBOARD`)
- **Trace Disk** (`TRACE_DISK`)
- **Trace Other** (`TRACE_MISC`)

Settings persist across app restarts via `SharedPreferences` (`xtulator_prefs`), restored in `onCreate()` after `nativeInit()` and saved in `onPause()`.

### 5. Hot-path logging removed

- `LOGI("Injecting scancode=0x%02X", sc)` → now `LOGKEY(...)` (TRACE_FLAG_KEYBOARD, off by default)
- `LOGE("nativeRun: loop %u, IP=...")` → now `LOGCPU(...)` (TRACE_FLAG_CPU, off by default)
- `nativeKeyDown`/`nativeKeyUp` logging → now `LOGKEY(...)` (off by default)
- `utility_loadFile` direct `__android_log_print` calls → gated on `TRACE_FLAG_MISC`
- Java `Log.i()` in `dispatchKeyEvent` → removed entirely (was on every key event)
- Java `Log.e()` in `onResume` → removed from the emulator thread path

### 6. Menu button fix

**Before:** `onKeyDown()` unconditionally called `nativeKeyDown(keyCode)` for all keys including MENU (keyCode 82), which mapped to scancode 0x01 (ESC) in the emulator. The MENU button was simultaneously trying to show the options menu AND send ESC to the emulation.

**After:** `onKeyDown()`/`onKeyUp()` now check `if (keyCode != KeyEvent.KEYCODE_MENU && keyCode != KeyEvent.KEYCODE_BACK)` before forwarding to native — MENU/BACK are exclusively system keys for the options menu. The `dispatchKeyEvent` already handled this correctly, but `onKeyDown`/`onKeyUp` were the gap that let MENU leak through to the emulator.

`i8259_nextintr`:
```c
uint8_t i8259_nextintr(I8259_t* i8259) {
    uint8_t i, tmpirr;
    tmpirr = i8259->irr & (~i8259->imr);
    for (i = 0; i < 8; i++)
        if ((tmpirr >> i) & 1) {
            i8259->irr &= ~(1 << i);
            i8259->isr |= (1 << i);
            return(i8259->icw[2] + i);
        }
    return 0;
}
```

This finds the lowest-numbered pending interrupt. For IRQ1 (keyboard), it returns `i8259->icw[2] + 1 = 8 + 1 = 9`.

`cpu_intcall` then executes the interrupt handler at vector 9. The BIOS sets up the interrupt vector table during POST. The IRQ1 handler (INT 9) reads port 0x60 to get the scancode.

FUNC_INLINE void cpu_intcall(CPU_t* cpu, uint8_t intnum) {
    if (cpu->int_callback[intnum] != NULL) {
        (*cpu->int_callback[intnum])(cpu, intnum);
        return;
    }

    push(cpu, makeflagsword(cpu));
    push(cpu, cpu->segregs[regcs]);
    push(cpu, cpu->ip);
    cpu->segregs[regcs] = getmem16(cpu, 0, (uint16_t)intnum * 4 + 2);
    cpu->ip = getmem16(cpu, 0, (uint16_t)intnum * 4);
    cpu->ifl = 0;
    cpu->tf = 0;
}
```

1. If `cpu->int_callback[intnum]` is not NULL, call the callback
2. Otherwise, do the standard interrupt handling (push flags, CS, IP, load CS:IP from IVT, clear IF and TF)

uint8_t i8259_nextintr(I8259_t* i8259) {
    uint8_t i, tmpirr;
    tmpirr = i8259->irr & (~i8259->imr);
    for (i = 0; i < 8; i++)
        if ((tmpirr >> i) & 1) {
            i8259->irr &= ~(1 << i);
            i8259->isr |= (1 << i);
            return(i8259->icw[2] + i);
        }
    return 0;
}
```

For IRR bit 1: `i = 1`, returns `i8259->icw[2] + 1 = 8 + 1 = 9`. ✓

    for (loopcount = 0; loopcount < execloops; loopcount++) {
        // Hot-address sample
        if (trace_flags & TRACE_FLAG_CPU && (loopcount & 0xFF) == 0) {
            cpu_profile_add(...);

        } else {

        }

        // Execute one instruction

        cpu->segoverride = 0;
        cpu->useseg = cpu->segregs[regds];
        docontinue = 0;

    }
}

}

115: uint8_t biosdisk_read(CPU_t* cpu, uint8_t drivenum, uint16_t dstseg, uint16_t dstoff, uint16_t cyl, uint16_t sect, uint16_t head, uint16_t sectcount) {
116: 	uint32_t memdest, lba, fileoffset, cursect, sectoffset;
117: 	static uint32_t dbg_count = 0;
118: 	/* Log the first few requests and then every 64th: the FreeDOS boot sector
119: 	   spins here forever when a read fails, so one line per attempt would be
120: 	   thousands of lines per second. */
121: 	uint8_t dbg = (dbg_count < 4) || ((dbg_count & 63) == 0);
122: 	dbg_count++;
123: 
124: 	if (!sect || !biosdisk[drivenum].inserted) {
125: 		if (dbg) DIAG("BIOSDISK: REJECT drive=%u sect=%u inserted=%u (fileoffset not computed)", drivenum, sect, biosdisk[drivenum].inserted);
126: 		return 1;
127: 	}
128: 	lba = ((uint32_t)cyl * (uint32_t)biosdisk[drivenum].heads + (uint32_t)head) * (uint32_t)biosdisk[drivenum].sects + (uint32_t)sect - 1UL;
129: 	fileoffset = lba * 512UL;
130: 	if (fileoffset > biosdisk[drivenum].filesize) {
131: 		if (dbg) DIAG("BIOSDISK: PAST-EOF drive=%u chs=%u/%u/%u lba=%u offset=%u filesize=%u", drivenum, cyl, head, sect, lba, fileoffset, biosdisk[drivenum].filesize);
132: 		return 1;
133: 	}
134: 	
135: 	/* Always log boot sector reads (cyl=0, head=0, sect=1) */
136: 	if (cyl == 0 && head == 0 && sect == 1) {
137: 		DIAG("BIOSDISK: BOOT SECTOR READ drive=%u chs=%u/%u/%u count=%u -> %04X:%04X lba=%u filesize=%u geom=%ux%ux%u",
138: 			drivenum, cyl, head, sect, sectcount, dstseg, dstoff, lba, biosdisk[drivenum].filesize,
139: 			biosdisk[drivenum].cyls, biosdisk[drivenum].heads, biosdisk[drivenum].sects);
140: 	}
141: 	
142: 	fseek(biosdisk[drivenum].diskfile, fileoffset, SEEK_SET);
143: 	memdest = ((uint32_t)dstseg << 4) + (uint32_t)dstoff;
144: 	for (cursect = 0; cursect < sectcount; cursect++) {
145: 		if (fread(biosdisk_sectbuf, 1, 512, biosdisk[drivenum].diskfile) < 512) break;
146: 		for (sectoffset = 0; sectoffset < 512; sectoffset++) {
147: 			cpu_write(cpu, memdest++, biosdisk_sectbuf[sectoffset]);
148: 		}
149: 	}
150: 	if (dbg) DIAG("BIOSDISK: read drive=%u chs=%u/%u/%u count=%u -> %04X:%04X lba=%u read=%u/%u geom=%ux%ux%u size=%u",
151: 		drivenum, cyl, head, sect, sectcount, dstseg, dstoff, lba, cursect, sectcount,
152: 		biosdisk[drivenum].cyls, biosdisk[drivenum].heads, biosdisk[drivenum].sects,
153: 		biosdisk[drivenum].filesize);
154: 	cpu->regs.byteregs[regal] = cursect;
155: 	cpu->cf = 0;
156: 	cpu->regs.byteregs[regah] = 0;
157: 	return 0;
158: }

160: uint8_t biosdisk_write(CPU_t* cpu, uint8_t drivenum, uint16_t dstseg, uint16_t dstoff, uint16_t cyl, uint16_t sect, uint16_t head, uint16_t sectcount) {
161: 	uint32_t memdest, lba, fileoffset, cursect, sectoffset;
162: 	if (!sect || !biosdisk[drivenum].inserted) return 1;
163: 	lba = ((uint32_t)cyl * (uint32_t)biosdisk[drivenum].heads + (uint32_t)head) * (uint32_t)biosdisk[drivenum].sects + (uint32_t)sect - 1UL;
164: 	fileoffset = lba * 512UL;
165: 	if (fileoffset > biosdisk[drivenum].filesize) return 1;
166: 	fseek(biosdisk[drivenum].diskfile, fileoffset, SEEK_SET);
167: 	memdest = ((uint32_t)dstseg << 4) + (uint32_t)dstoff;
168: 	for (cursect = 0; cursect < sectcount; cursect++) {
169: 		for (sectoffset = 0; sectoffset < 512; sectoffset++) {
170: 			biosdisk_sectbuf[sectoffset] = cpu_read(cpu, memdest++);
171: 		}
172: 		fwrite(biosdisk_sectbuf, 1, 512, biosdisk[drivenum].diskfile);
173: 	}
174: 	cpu->regs.byteregs[regal] = (uint8_t)sectcount;
175: 	cpu->cf = 0;
176: 	cpu->regs.byteregs[regah] = 0;
177: 	return 0;
178: }

## Objective
- Add per-category logging toggles (cpu / keyboard / disk) to an Android x86 emulator (XTulator) and fix the keyboard and menu button which are broken due to excessive logd blocking on a single-core ARMv5TE target (SHARP IS01, Android 1.6).

## Important Details
- Root cause of slowdown was `volatile uint8_t xt_trace_enabled = 1` in `debuglog.c:36` — hardcoded ON, every `__android_log_print` call (0.5–2ms blocking write to logd) activated in hot paths: IRQ raise/ack (`i8259.c`), timer callbacks (`i8253.c`), framebuffer copy every frame (`android_frontend.c`), key injection (`jni_bridge.c`).
- NDK defines `__ANDROID__` (double underscore), but 4 files used `#ifdef ANDROID` — logging was silently compiled out on Android builds. Fixed to `#ifdef __ANDROID__`.
- `trace_flags` bitmask replaces single boolean; defaults to `0x00` (all off).
- Trace categories: `TRACE_FLAG_CPU=0x01`, `TRACE_FLAG_KEYBOARD=0x02`, `TRACE_FLAG_DISK=0x04`, `TRACE_FLAG_TIMERS=0x08`, `TRACE_FLAG_INTERRUPTS=0x10`, `TRACE_FLAG_VIDEO=0x20`, `TRACE_FLAG_MISC=0x40`, `TRACE_FLAG_DIAG=0x80`.
- Build path is Docker-based (`/src/android/...`), NDK r10e-era, API 4, armeabi, `APP_STL := gnustl_static`, `-D__ANDROID__ -O2 -g -std=gnu99`, `-llog -lm`.
- The `XtulatorActivity` extends `Activity` (not `NativeActivity`); native methods are called via JNI from a Java `Thread` (`mEmulatorThread`) that calls `nativeRun()`.
- Physical MENU button on IS01 = hardware key; `adb shell input keyevent KEYCODE_S` also should work.
- The emulator uses `instructionsperloop = 100000` on Android (no throttling; `limitCPU=0`), draining one scancode per outer-loop iteration.
- BIOS ROM: `roms/machine/xi8088/bios128k-2.0.bin`; IRQ1 vector = INT 9 (8259 `intoffset=8`, IRQ1 → vector 9).

- Updated all 11 module logging macros to use per-category `trace_flags & TRACE_FLAG_*` bits: `jni_bridge.c` (LOGI/LOGE/LOGW→MISC, new LOGKEY→KEYBOARD, LOGCPU→CPU), `machine.c` (MACHINE_LOGI→MISC + direct ref), `timing.c` (TIMING_LOGI→TIMERS), `biosdisk.c` (BIOSDISK_LOGI→DISK), `i8253.c` (I8253_LOGI→TIMERS), `i8259.c` (I8259_LOGI→INTERRUPTS), `vga.c` (VGA_LOGI→VIDEO), `utility.c` (UTIL_LOGI→MISC + direct refs), `android_audio.c` (AUDIO_LOGI/AUDIO_LOGE→MISC + direct ref), `android_frontend.c` (ANDROID_LOGI→VIDEO + added include of debuglog.h).

52: 		i8255->kbc_status |= 0x01;
53: #ifdef DEBUG_PPI
54: 		debug_log(DEBUG_INFO, "[KBC] Interface test\r\n");
55: #endif
56: 		break;
57: 	case 0xAD:
58: 		i8255->kbc_status |= 0x10;
59: #ifdef DEBUG_PPI
60: 		debug_log(DEBUG_INFO, "[KBC] Disable keyboard interface\r\n");
61: #endif
62: 		break;
63: 	case 0xAE:
64: 		i8255->kbc_status &= ~0x10;

80: 		i8255->kbc_status |= 0x01;

120: uint8_t i8255_readport(I8255_t* i8255, uint16_t portnum) {
121: #ifdef DEBUG_PPI
122: 	debug_log(DEBUG_INFO, "[I8255] Read port %02X\r\n", portnum);
123: #endif
124: 	portnum &= 7;
125: 	switch (portnum) {
126: 	case 0:
127: 		if (i8255->kbc_has_response) {
128: 			uint8_t response = i8255->kbc_response;
129: 			i8255->kbc_has_response = 0;
130: 			i8255->kbc_status &= ~0x01;
131: #ifdef DEBUG_PPI
132: 			debug_log(DEBUG_INFO, "[KBC] Port 60 read response: %02X\r\n", response);
133: #endif
134: 			return response;
135: 		}
136: 		if (i8255->keystate->isNew) {
137: 			uint8_t sc = i8255->keystate->scancode;
138: 			i8255->keystate->isNew = 0;
139: #ifdef DEBUG_PPI
140: 			debug_log(DEBUG_INFO, "[I8255] Port 60 read: scancode=%02X\r\n", sc);
141: #endif
142: 			return sc;
143: 		}
144: 		return 0xFF;
145: 	case 1:
146: 		return i8255->portB;
147: 	case 2:
148: 		if (i8255->portB & 8) {
149: 			return i8255->sw2 >> 4;
150: 		} else {
151: 			return i8255->sw2 & 0x0F;
152: 		}
153: 	case 4:
154: 		return (i8255->kbc_has_response || i8255->keystate->isNew) ? 0x01 : 0x00;
155: 	case 5:
156: 		return i8255->kbc_status;
157: 	}
158: 	return 0xFF;
159: }
160: 
161: void i8255_writeport(I8255_t* i8255, uint16_t portnum, uint8_t value) {
162: #ifdef DEBUG_PPI
163: 	debug_log(DEBUG_DETAIL, "[I8255] Write port %02X <- %02X\r\n", portnum, value);
164: #endif
165: 	portnum &= 7;
166: 	switch (portnum) {
167: 	case 0:
168: 		if (i8255->kbc_expect_data) {
169: #ifdef DEBUG_PPI
170: 			debug_log(DEBUG_INFO, "[KBC] Data for command: %02X\r\n", value);
171: #endif
172: 			i8255->kbc_expect_data = 0;
173: 		} else {
174: 			i8255->keystate->scancode = value;
175: #ifdef DEBUG_PPI
176: 			debug_log(DEBUG_INFO, "[KBC] Port 60 write (to keyboard): %02X\r\n", value);
177: #endif
178: 		}
179: 		break;
180: 	case 1:
181: 		if (value & 0x01) {
182: 			pcspeaker_selectGate(i8255->pcspeaker, PC_SPEAKER_USE_TIMER2);
183: #ifdef DEBUG_PPI
184: 			debug_log(DEBUG_DETAIL, "[I8255] Speaker take input from timer 2\r\n");
185: #endif
186: 		} else {
187: 			pcspeaker_selectGate(i8255->pcspeaker, PC_SPEAKER_USE_DIRECT);
188: #ifdef DEBUG_PPI
189: 			debug_log(DEBUG_DETAIL, "[I8255] Speaker take input from direct\r\n");
190: #endif
191: 		}
192: 		pcspeaker_setGateState(i8255->pcspeaker, PC_SPEAKER_GATE_DIRECT, (value >> 1) & 1);
193: #ifdef DEBUG_PPI
194: 		debug_log(DEBUG_DETAIL, "[I8255] Speaker direct value = %u\r\n", (value >> 1) & 1);
195: #endif
196: 		if ((value & 0x40) && !(i8255->portB & 0x40)) {
197: 			i8255->keystate->scancode = 0xAA;
198: #ifdef DEBUG_PPI
199: 			debug_log(DEBUG_DETAIL, "[I8255] Keyboard reset\r\n");
200: #endif
201: 		}
202: 		i8255->portB = (value & 0xEF) | (i8255->portB & 0x10);
203: 		break;
204: 	case 4:
205: 		kbc_process_command(i8255, value);
206: 		break;
207: 	}
208: }

229: }

54: FUNC_INLINE void flag_szp8(CPU_t* cpu, uint8_t value) {
55: 	if (!value) {

57: 	}
58: 	else {

60: 	}
61:

64: 	}
65: 	else {

69: 	cpu->pf = parity[value]; /* retrieve parity state from lookup table */
70: }

102: FUNC_INLINE void flag_adc8(CPU_t* cpu, uint8_t v1, uint8_t v2, uint8_t v3) {
103: 
104: 	/* v1 = destination operand, v2 = source operand, v3 = carry flag */
105: 	uint16_t	dst;
106: 
107: 	dst = (uint16_t)v1 + (uint16_t)v2 + (uint16_t)v3;
108: 	flag_szp8(cpu, (uint8_t)dst);
109: 	if (((dst ^ v1) & (dst ^ v2) & 0x80) == 0x80) {
110: 		cpu->of = 1;

112: 	else {

124: 		cpu->af = 1;
125: 	}
126: 	else {
127: 		cpu->af = 0; /* set or clear auxilliary flag */
128: 	}
129: }

403: FUNC_INLINE void getea(CPU_t* cpu, uint8_t rmval) {
404: 	uint32_t	tempea;
405: 
406: 	tempea = 0;
407: 	switch (cpu->mode) {
408: 	case 0:
409: 		switch (rmval) {
410: 		case 0:
411: 			tempea = cpu->regs.wordregs[regbx] + cpu->regs.wordregs[regsi];
412: 			break;
413: 		case 1:
414: 			tempea = cpu->regs.wordregs[regbx] + cpu->regs.wordregs[regdi];
415: 			break;
416: 		case 2:
417: 			tempea = cpu->regs.wordregs[regbp] + cpu->regs.wordregs[regsi];
418: 			break;
419: 		case 3:
420: 			tempea = cpu->regs.wordregs[regbp] + cpu->regs.wordregs[regdi];
421: 			break;
422: 		case 4:
423: 			tempea = cpu->regs.wordregs[regsi];
424: 			break;
425: 		case 5:
426: 			tempea = cpu->regs.wordregs[regdi];
427: 			break;
428: 		case 6:
429: 			tempea = cpu->disp16;
430: 			break;
431: 		case 7:
432: 			tempea = cpu->regs.wordregs[regbx];
433: 			break;
434: 		}
435: 		break;
436: 
437: 	case 1:
438: 	case 2:
439: 		switch (rmval) {
440: 		case 0:
441: 			tempea = cpu->regs.wordregs[regbx] + cpu->regs.wordregs[regsi] + cpu->disp16;
442: 			break;
443: 		case 1:
444: 			tempea = cpu->regs.wordregs[regbx] + cpu->regs.wordregs[regdi] + cpu->disp16;
445: 			break;
446: 		case 2:
447: 			tempea = cpu->regs.wordregs[regbp] + cpu->regs.wordregs[regsi] + cpu->disp16;
448: 			break;
449: 		case 3:
450: 			tempea = cpu->regs.wordregs[regbp] + cpu->regs.wordregs[regdi] + cpu->disp16;
451: 			break;
452: 		case 4:
453: 			tempea = cpu->regs.wordregs[regsi] + cpu->disp16;
454: 			break;
455: 		case 5:
456: 			tempea = cpu->regs.wordregs[regdi] + cpu->disp16;
457: 			break;
458: 		case 6:
459: 			tempea = cpu->regs.wordregs[regbp] + cpu->disp16;
460: 			break;
461: 		case 7:
462: 			tempea = cpu->regs.wordregs[regbx] + cpu->disp16;
463: 			break;
464: 		}
465: 		break;
466: 	}
467: 
468: 	cpu->ea = (tempea & 0xFFFF) + (cpu->useseg << 4);
469: }

537: FUNC_INLINE uint8_t op_grp2_8(CPU_t* cpu, uint8_t cnt) {
538: 
539: 	uint16_t	s;
540: 	uint16_t	shift;
541: 	uint16_t	oldcf;
542: 	uint16_t	msb;
543: 
544: 	s = cpu->oper1b;
545: 	oldcf = cpu->cf;
546: #ifdef CPU_LIMIT_SHIFT_COUNT
547: 	cnt &= 0x1F;
548: #endif
549: 	switch (cpu->reg) {
550: 	case 0: /* ROL r/m8 */
551: 		for (shift = 1; shift <= cnt; shift++) {
552: 			if (s & 0x80) {
553: 				cpu->cf = 1;
554: 			}
555: 			else {
556: 				cpu->cf = 0;
557: 			}
558: 
559: 			s = s << 1;
560: 			s = s | cpu->cf;
561: 		}
562: 
563: 		if (cnt == 1) {
564: 			//cpu->of = cpu->cf ^ ( (s >> 7) & 1);
565: 			if ((s & 0x80) && cpu->cf) cpu->of = 1; else cpu->of = 0;
566: 		}
567: 		else cpu->of = 0;
568: 		break;
569: 
570: 	case 1: /* ROR r/m8 */
571: 		for (shift = 1; shift <= cnt; shift++) {
572: 			cpu->cf = s & 1;
573: 			s = (s >> 1) | (cpu->cf << 7);
574: 		}
575: 
576: 		if (cnt == 1) {
577: 			cpu->of = (s >> 7) ^ ((s >> 6) & 1);
578: 		}
579: 		break;
580: 
581: 	case 2: /* RCL r/m8 */
582: 		for (shift = 1; shift <= cnt; shift++) {
583: 			oldcf = cpu->cf;
584: 			if (s & 0x80) {
585: 				cpu->cf = 1;
586: 			}
587: 			else {
588: 				cpu->cf = 0;
589: 			}
590: 
591: 			s = s << 1;
592: 			s = s | oldcf;
593: 		}
594: 
595: 		if (cnt == 1) {
596: 			cpu->of = cpu->cf ^ ((s >> 7) & 1);
597: 		}
598: 		break;
599: 
600: 	case 3: /* RCR r/m8 */
601: 		for (shift = 1; shift <= cnt; shift++) {
602: 			oldcf = cpu->cf;
603: 			cpu->cf = s & 1;
604: 			s = (s >> 1) | (oldcf << 7);
605: 		}
606: 
607: 		if (cnt == 1) {
608: 			cpu->of = (s >> 7) ^ ((s >> 6) & 1);
609: 		}
610: 		break;
611: 
612: 	case 4:
613: 	case 6: /* SHL r/m8 */
614: 		for (shift = 1; shift <= cnt; shift++) {
615: 			if (s & 0x80) {
616: 				cpu->cf = 1;
617: 			}
618: 			else {
619: 				cpu->cf = 0;
620: 			}
621: 
622: 			s = (s << 1) & 0xFF;
623: 		}
624: 
625: 		if ((cnt == 1) && (cpu->cf == (s >> 7))) {
626: 			cpu->of = 0;
627: 		}
628: 		else {
629: 			cpu->of = 1;
630: 		}
631: 
632: 		flag_szp8(cpu, (uint8_t)s);
633: 		break;
634: 
635: 	case 5: /* SHR r/m8 */
636: 		if ((cnt == 1) && (s & 0x80)) {
637: 			cpu->of = 1;
638: 		}
639: 		else {
640: 			cpu->of = 0;
641: 		}
642: 
643: 		for (shift = 1; shift <= cnt; shift++) {
644: 			cpu->cf = s & 1;
645: 			s = s >> 1;
646: 		}
647: 
648: 		flag_szp8(cpu, (uint8_t)s);
649: 		break;
650: 
651: 	case 7: /* SAR r/m8 */
652: 		for (shift = 1; shift <= cnt; shift++) {
653: 			msb = s & 0x80;
654: 			cpu->cf = s & 1;
655: 			s = (s >> 1) | msb;
656: 		}
657: 
658: 		cpu->of = 0;
659: 		flag_szp8(cpu, (uint8_t)s);
660: 		break;
661: 	}
662: 
663: 	return s & 0xFF;
664: }
665: 
666: FUNC_INLINE uint16_t op_grp2_16(CPU_t* cpu, uint8_t cnt) {
667: 
668: 	uint32_t	s;
669: 	uint32_t	shift;
670: 	uint32_t	oldcf;
671: 	uint32_t	msb;
672: 
673: 	s = cpu->oper1;
674: 	oldcf = cpu->cf;
675: #ifdef CPU_LIMIT_SHIFT_COUNT
676: 	cnt &= 0x1F;
677: #endif
678: 	switch (cpu->reg) {
679: 	case 0: /* ROL r/m8 */
680: 		for (shift = 1; shift <= cnt; shift++) {
681: 			if (s & 0x8000) {
682: 				cpu->cf = 1;
683: 			}
684: 			else {
685: 				cpu->cf = 0;
686: 			}
687: 
688: 			s = s << 1;
689: 			s = s | cpu->cf;
690: 		}
691: 
692: 		if (cnt == 1) {
693: 			cpu->of = cpu->cf ^ ((s >> 15) & 1);
694: 		}
695: 		break;
696: 
697: 	case 1: /* ROR r/m8 */
698: 		for (shift = 1; shift <= cnt; shift++) {
699: 			cpu->cf = s & 1;
700: 			s = (s >> 1) | (cpu->cf << 15);
701: 		}
702: 
703: 		if (cnt == 1) {
704: 			cpu->of = (s >> 15) ^ ((s >> 14) & 1);
705: 		}
706: 		break;
707: 
708: 	case 2: /* RCL r/m8 */
709: 		for (shift = 1; shift <= cnt; shift++) {
710: 			oldcf = cpu->cf;
711: 			if (s & 0x8000) {
712: 				cpu->cf = 1;
713: 			}
714: 			else {
715: 				cpu->cf = 0;
716: 			}
717: 
718: 			s = s << 1;
719: 			s = s | oldcf;
720: 		}
721: 
722: 		if (cnt == 1) {
723: 			cpu->of = cpu->cf ^ ((s >> 15) & 1);
724: 		}
725: 		break;
726: 
727: 	case 3: /* RCR r/m8 */
728: 		for (shift = 1; shift <= cnt; shift++) {
729: 			oldcf = cpu->cf;
730: 			cpu->cf = s & 1;
731: 			s = (s >> 1) | (oldcf << 15);
732: 		}
733: 
734: 		if (cnt == 1) {
735: 			cpu->of = (s >> 15) ^ ((s >> 14) & 1);
736: 		}
737: 		break;
738: 
739: 	case 4:
740: 	case 6: /* SHL r/m8 */
741: 		for (shift = 1; shift <= cnt; shift++) {
742: 			if (s & 0x8000) {
743: 				cpu->cf = 1;
744: 			}
745: 			else {
746: 				cpu->cf = 0;
747: 			}
748: 
749: 			s = (s << 1) & 0xFFFF;
750: 		}
751: 
752: 		if ((cnt == 1) && (cpu->cf == (s >> 15))) {
753: 			cpu->of = 0;
754: 		}
755: 		else {
756: 			cpu->of = 1;
757: 		}
758: 
759: 		flag_szp16(cpu, (uint16_t)s);
760: 		break;
761: 
762: 	case 5: /* SHR r/m8 */
763: 		if ((cnt == 1) && (s & 0x8000)) {
764: 			cpu->of = 1;
765: 		}
766: 		else {
767: 			cpu->of = 0;
768: 		}
769: 
770: 		for (shift = 1; shift <= cnt; shift++) {
771: 			cpu->cf = s & 1;
772: 			s = s >> 1;
773: 		}
774: 
775: 		flag_szp16(cpu, (uint16_t)s);
776: 		break;
777: 
778: 	case 7: /* SAR r/m8 */
779: 		for (shift = 1; shift <= cnt; shift++) {
780: 			msb = s & 0x8000;
781: 			cpu->cf = s & 1;
782: 			s = (s >> 1) | msb;
783: 		}
784: 
785: 		cpu->of = 0;
786: 		flag_szp16(cpu, (uint16_t)s);
787: 		break;
788: 	}
789: 
790: 	return (uint16_t)s & 0xFFFF;
791: }

793: FUNC_INLINE void op_div8(CPU_t* cpu, uint16_t valdiv, uint8_t divisor) {
794: 	if (divisor == 0) {
795: 		cpu_intcall(cpu, 0);
796: 		return;
797: 	}
798: 
799: 	if ((valdiv / (uint16_t)divisor) > 0xFF) {
800: 		cpu_intcall(cpu, 0);
801: 		return;
802: 	}
803: 
804: 	cpu->regs.byteregs[regah] = valdiv % (uint16_t)divisor;
805: 	cpu->regs.byteregs[regal] = valdiv / (uint16_t)divisor;
806: }
807: 
808: FUNC_INLINE void op_idiv8(CPU_t* cpu, uint16_t valdiv, uint8_t divisor) {
809: 	//TODO: Rewrite IDIV code, I wrote this in 2011. It can be made far more efficient.
810: 	uint16_t	s1;
811: 	uint16_t	s2;
812: 	uint16_t	d1;
813: 	uint16_t	d2;
814: 	int	sign;
815: 
816: 	if (divisor == 0) {
817: 		cpu_intcall(cpu, 0);
818: 		return;
819: 	}
820: 
821: 	s1 = valdiv;
822: 	s2 = divisor;
823: 	sign = (((s1 ^ s2) & 0x8000) != 0);
824: 	s1 = (s1 < 0x8000) ? s1 : ((~s1 + 1) & 0xffff);
825: 	s2 = (s2 < 0x8000) ? s2 : ((~s2 + 1) & 0xffff);
826: 	d1 = s1 / s2;
827: 	d2 = s1 % s2;
828: 	if (d1 & 0xFF00) {
829: 		cpu_intcall(cpu, 0);
830: 		return;
831: 	}
832: 
833: 	if (sign) {
834: 		d1 = (~d1 + 1) & 0xff;
835: 		d2 = (~d2 + 1) & 0xff;
836: 	}
837: 
838: 	cpu->regs.byteregs[regah] = (uint8_t)d2;
839: 	cpu->regs.byteregs[regal] = (uint8_t)d1;
840: }

842: FUNC_INLINE void op_grp3_8(CPU_t* cpu) {
843: 	cpu->oper1 = signext(cpu->oper1b);
844: 	cpu->oper2 = signext(cpu->oper2b);
845: 	switch (cpu->reg) {
846: 	case 0:
847: 	case 1: /* TEST */
848: 		flag_log8(cpu, cpu->oper1b & getmem8(cpu, cpu->segregs[regcs], cpu->ip));
849: 		StepIP(cpu, 1);
850: 		break;
851: 
852: 	case 2: /* NOT */
853: 		cpu->res8 = ~cpu->oper1b;
854: 		break;
855: 
856: 	case 3: /* NEG */
857: 		cpu->res8 = (~cpu->oper1b) + 1;
858: 		flag_sub8(cpu, 0, cpu->oper1b);
859: 		if (cpu->res8 == 0) {
860: 			cpu->cf = 0;
861: 		}
862: 		else {
863: 			cpu->cf = 1;
864: 		}
865: 		break;
866: 
867: 	case 4: /* MUL */
868: 		cpu->temp1 = (uint32_t)cpu->oper1b * (uint32_t)cpu->regs.byteregs[regal];
869: 		cpu->regs.wordregs[regax] = cpu->temp1 & 0xFFFF;
870: 		flag_szp8(cpu, (uint8_t)cpu->temp1);
871: 		if (cpu->regs.byteregs[regah]) {
872: 			cpu->cf = 1;
873: 			cpu->of = 1;
874: 		}
875: 		else {
876: 			cpu->cf = 0;
877: 			cpu->of = 0;
878: 		}
879: #ifdef CPU_CLEAR_ZF_ON_MUL
880: 		cpu->zf = 0;
881: #endif
882: 		break;
883: 
884: 	case 5: /* IMUL */
885: 		cpu->oper1 = signext(cpu->oper1b);
886: 		cpu->temp1 = signext(cpu->regs.byteregs[regal]);
887: 		cpu->temp2 = cpu->oper1;
888: 		if ((cpu->temp1 & 0x80) == 0x80) {
889: 			cpu->temp1 = cpu->temp1 | 0xFFFFFF00;
890: 		}
891: 
892: 		if ((cpu->temp2 & 0x80) == 0x80) {
893: 			cpu->temp2 = cpu->temp2 | 0xFFFFFF00;
894: 		}
895: 
896: 		cpu->temp3 = (cpu->temp1 * cpu->temp2) & 0xFFFF;
897: 		cpu->regs.wordregs[regax] = cpu->temp3 & 0xFFFF;
898: 		if (cpu->regs.byteregs[regah]) {
899: 			cpu->cf = 1;
900: 			cpu->of = 1;
901: 		}
902: 		else {
903: 			cpu->cf = 0;
904: 			cpu->of = 0;
905: 		}
906: #ifdef CPU_CLEAR_ZF_ON_MUL
907: 		cpu->zf = 0;
908: #endif
909: 		break;
910: 
911: 	case 6: /* DIV */
912: 		op_div8(cpu, cpu->regs.wordregs[regax], cpu->oper1b);
913: 		break;
914: 
915: 	case 7: /* IDIV */
916: 		op_idiv8(cpu, cpu->regs.wordregs[regax], cpu->oper1b);
917: 		break;
918: 	}
919: }

926: 
927: 	if ((valdiv / (uint32_t)divisor) > 0xFFFF) {

930: 	}
931: 
932: 	cpu->regs.wordregs[regdx] = valdiv % (uint32_t)divisor;

936: FUNC_INLINE void op_idiv16(CPU_t* cpu, uint32_t valdiv, uint16_t divisor) {
937: 	//TODO: Rewrite IDIV code, I wrote this in 2011. It can be made far more efficient.
938: 	uint32_t	d1;
939: 	uint32_t	d2;
940: 	uint32_t	s1;
941: 	uint32_t	s2;
942: 	int	sign;

944: 	if (divisor == 0) {

947: 	}
948: 
949: 	s1 = valdiv;
950: 	s2 = divisor;
951: 	s2 = (s2 & 0x8000) ? (s2 | 0xffff0000) : s2;
952: 	sign = (((s1 ^ s2) & 0x80000000) != 0);
953: 	s1 = (s1 < 0x80000000) ? s1 : ((~s1 + 1) & 0xffffffff);
954: 	s2 = (s2 < 0x80000000) ? s2 : ((~s2 + 1) & 0xffffffff);

966: 
967: 	cpu->regs.wordregs[regax] = d1;

971: FUNC_INLINE void op_grp3_16(CPU_t* cpu) {
972: 	switch (cpu->reg) {
973: 	case 0:
974: 	case 1: /* TEST */
975: 		flag_log16(cpu, cpu->oper1 & getmem16(cpu, cpu->segregs[regcs], cpu->ip));
976: 		StepIP(cpu, 2);
977: 		break;
978: 
979: 	case 2: /* NOT */
980: 		cpu->res16 = ~cpu->oper1;
981: 		break;
982: 
983: 	case 3: /* NEG */
984: 		cpu->res16 = (~cpu->oper1) + 1;
985: 		flag_sub16(cpu, 0, cpu->oper1);
986: 		if (cpu->res16) {
987: 			cpu->cf = 1;
988: 		}
989: 		else {
990: 			cpu->cf = 0;
991: 		}
992: 		break;
993: 
994: 	case 4: /* MUL */
995: 		cpu->temp1 = (uint32_t)cpu->oper1 * (uint32_t)cpu->regs.wordregs[regax];
996: 		cpu->regs.wordregs[regax] = cpu->temp1 & 0xFFFF;
997: 		cpu->regs.wordregs[regdx] = cpu->temp1 >> 16;
998: 		flag_szp16(cpu, (uint16_t)cpu->temp1);
999: 		if (cpu->regs.wordregs[regdx]) {
1000: 			cpu->cf = 1;
1001: 			cpu->of = 1;
1002: 		}
1003: 		else {
1004: 			cpu->cf = 0;
1005: 			cpu->of = 0;
1006: 		}
1007: #ifdef CPU_CLEAR_ZF_ON_MUL
1008: 		cpu->zf = 0;
1009: #endif
1010: 		break;
1011: 
1012: 	case 5: /* IMUL */
1013: 		cpu->temp1 = cpu->regs.wordregs[regax];
1014: 		cpu->temp2 = cpu->oper1;
1015: 		if (cpu->temp1 & 0x8000) {
1016: 			cpu->temp1 |= 0xFFFF0000;
1017: 		}
1018: 
1019: 		if (cpu->temp2 & 0x8000) {
1020: 			cpu->temp2 |= 0xFFFF0000;
1021: 		}
1022: 
1023: 		cpu->temp3 = cpu->temp1 * cpu->temp2;
1024: 		cpu->regs.wordregs[regax] = cpu->temp3 & 0xFFFF;	/* into register ax */
1025: 		cpu->regs.wordregs[regdx] = cpu->temp3 >> 16;	/* into register dx */
1026: 		if (cpu->regs.wordregs[regdx]) {
1027: 			cpu->cf = 1;
1028: 			cpu->of = 1;
1029: 		}
1030: 		else {
1031: 			cpu->cf = 0;
1032: 			cpu->of = 0;
1033: 		}
1034: #ifdef CPU_CLEAR_ZF_ON_MUL
1035: 		cpu->zf = 0;
1036: #endif
1037: 		break;
1038: 
1039: 	case 6: /* DIV */
1040: 		op_div16(cpu, ((uint32_t)cpu->regs.wordregs[regdx] << 16) + cpu->regs.wordregs[regax], cpu->oper1);
1041: 		break;
1042: 
1043: 	case 7: /* DIV */
1044: 		op_idiv16(cpu, ((uint32_t)cpu->regs.wordregs[regdx] << 16) + cpu->regs.wordregs[regax], cpu->oper1);
1045: 		break;
1046: 	}
1047: }

1049: FUNC_INLINE void op_grp5(CPU_t* cpu) {
1050: 	switch (cpu->reg) {
1051: 	case 0: /* INC Ev */
1052: 		cpu->oper2 = 1;
1053: 		cpu->tempcf = cpu->cf;
1054: 		op_add16(cpu);
1055: 		cpu->cf = cpu->tempcf;
1056: 		writerm16(cpu, cpu->rm, cpu->res16);
1057: 		break;
1058: 
1059: 	case 1: /* DEC Ev */
1060: 		cpu->oper2 = 1;
1061: 		cpu->tempcf = cpu->cf;
1062: 		op_sub16(cpu);
1063: 		cpu->cf = cpu->tempcf;
1064: 		writerm16(cpu, cpu->rm, cpu->res16);
1065: 		break;
1066: 
1067: 	case 2: /* CALL Ev */
1068: 		push(cpu, cpu->ip);
1069: 		cpu->ip = cpu->oper1;
1070: 		break;
1071: 
1072: 	case 3: /* CALL Mp */
1073: 		push(cpu, cpu->segregs[regcs]);
1074: 		push(cpu, cpu->ip);
1075: 		getea(cpu, cpu->rm);
1076: 		cpu->ip = (uint16_t)cpu_read(cpu, cpu->ea) + (uint16_t)cpu_read(cpu, cpu->ea + 1) * 256;
1077: 		cpu->segregs[regcs] = (uint16_t)cpu_read(cpu, cpu->ea + 2) + (uint16_t)cpu_read(cpu, cpu->ea + 3) * 256;
1078: 		break;
1079: 
1080: 	case 4: /* JMP Ev */
1081: 		cpu->ip = cpu->oper1;
1082: 		break;
1083: 
1084: 	case 5: /* JMP Mp */
1085: 		getea(cpu, cpu->rm);
1086: 		cpu->ip = (uint16_t)cpu_read(cpu, cpu->ea) + (uint16_t)cpu_read(cpu, cpu->ea + 1) * 256;
1087: 		cpu->segregs[regcs] = (uint16_t)cpu_read(cpu, cpu->ea + 2) + (uint16_t)cpu_read(cpu, cpu->ea + 3) * 256;
1088: 		break;
1089: 
1090: 	case 6: /* PUSH Ev */
1091: 		push(cpu, cpu->oper1);
1092: 		break;
1093: 	}
1094: }

1096: FUNC_INLINE void cpu_intcall(CPU_t* cpu, uint8_t intnum) {
1097: 	if (cpu->int_callback[intnum] != NULL) {
1098: 		(*cpu->int_callback[intnum])(cpu, intnum);
1099: 		return;
1100: 	}
1101: 
1102: 	push(cpu, makeflagsword(cpu));
1103: 	push(cpu, cpu->segregs[regcs]);
1104: 	push(cpu, cpu->ip);
1105: 	cpu->segregs[regcs] = getmem16(cpu, 0, (uint16_t)intnum * 4 + 2);
1106: 	cpu->ip = getmem16(cpu, 0, (uint16_t)intnum * 4);
1107: 	cpu->ifl = 0;
1108: 	cpu->tf = 0;
1109: }

1111: void cpu_interruptCheck(CPU_t* cpu, I8259_t* i8259) {
1112: 	/* get next interrupt from the i8259, if any */
1113: 	if (!cpu->trap_toggle && (cpu->ifl && (i8259->irr & (~i8259->imr)))) {
1114: 		cpu->hltstate = 0;
1115: 		cpu_intcall(cpu, i8259_nextintr(i8259));
1116: 	}
1117: }

1119: /* Exact-address hot table; see cpu.h. */
1120: static uint32_t prof_key[CPU_PROFILE_SLOTS];
1121: static uint32_t prof_cnt[CPU_PROFILE_SLOTS];
1122: static uint32_t prof_used = 0;
1123: static uint64_t prof_total = 0;
1124: 
1125: void cpu_profileReset(void) {
1126: 	memset(prof_key, 0, sizeof(prof_key));
1127: 	memset(prof_cnt, 0, sizeof(prof_cnt));
1128: 	prof_used = 0;
1129: 	prof_total = 0;
1130: }
1131: 
1132: static void cpu_profile_add(uint32_t linear) {
1133: 	uint32_t h = (linear * 2654435761u) >> 20;
1134: 	uint32_t i;
1135: 	for (i = 0; i < 64; i++) {
1136: 		uint32_t s = (h + i) & (CPU_PROFILE_SLOTS - 1);
1137: 		if (prof_cnt[s] == 0) {
1138: 			if (prof_used >= CPU_PROFILE_SLOTS) {
1139: 				return; /*table full, stop recording rather than thrash*/
1140: 			}
1141: 			prof_key[s] = linear;
1142: 			prof_cnt[s] = 1;
1143: 			prof_used++;
1144: 			prof_total++;
1145: 			return;
1146: 		}
1147: 		if (prof_key[s] == linear) {
1148: 			prof_cnt[s]++;
1149: 			prof_total++;
1150: 			return;
1151: 		}
1152: 	}
1153: }
1154: 
1155: void cpu_dumpmem(CPU_t* cpu, uint32_t linear, uint32_t len) {
1156: 	static const char hex[] = "0123456789ABCDEF";
1157: 	char row[64];
1158: 	uint32_t i, n;
1159: 	DIAG("MEM: dump %05X..%05X", linear, linear + len - 1);
1160: 	for (i = 0; i < len; i += 16) {
1161: 		n = (len - i < 16) ? (len - i) : 16;
1162: 		{
1163: 			uint32_t k;
1164: 			char addr[8];
1165: 			/* "%05X" by hand; the emulator has no snprintf dependency here. */
1166: 			for (k = 5; k-- > 0;) {
1167: 				addr[k] = hex[(linear + i) >> ((4 - k) * 4) & 0xF];
1168: 			}
1169: 			addr[5] = ':';
1170: 			for (k = 0; k < 6; k++) {
1171: 				row[k] = addr[k];
1172: 			}
1173: 		}
1174: 		{
1175: 			uint32_t k, o = 6;
1176: 			for (k = 0; k < n; k++) {
1177: 				uint8_t b = cpu_read(cpu, linear + i + k);
1178: 				row[o++] = hex[b >> 4];
1179: 				row[o++] = hex[b & 15];
1180: 			}
1181: 			row[o] = 0;
1182: 			DIAG("%s", row);
1183: 		}
1184: 	}
1185: }
1186: 
1187: uint32_t cpu_hottest(void) {
1188: 	uint32_t i, top = 0;
1189: 	for (i = 0; i < CPU_PROFILE_SLOTS; i++) {
1190: 		if (prof_cnt[i] > prof_cnt[top]) {
1191: 			top = i;
1192: 		}
1193: 	}
1194: 	return (prof_cnt[top] == 0) ? 0xFFFFFFFFu : prof_key[top];
1195: }
1196: 
1197: void cpu_profileDump(void) {
1198: 	uint32_t i, j, top;
1199: 	if (prof_total == 0) {
1200: 		DIAG("PROFILE: no samples");
1201: 		return;
1202: 	}
1203: 	DIAG("PROFILE: %llu samples, %u distinct addresses",
1204: 		(unsigned long long)prof_total, prof_used);
1205: 	for (j = 0; j < 12; j++) {
1206: 		top = 0;
1207: 		for (i = 0; i < CPU_PROFILE_SLOTS; i++) {
1208: 			if (prof_cnt[i] > prof_cnt[top]) {
1209: 				top = i;
1210: 			}
1211: 		}
1212: 		if (prof_cnt[top] == 0) {
1213: 			break;
1214: 		}
1215: 		DIAG("PROFILE:   %5.1f%%  linear %05X  (CS %04X IP %04X)",
1216: 			((double)prof_cnt[top] * 100.0) / (double)prof_total,
1217: 			prof_key[top], (uint16_t)(prof_key[top] >> 4), (uint16_t)(prof_key[top] & 0xF));
1218: 		prof_cnt[top] = 0; /*report each address once*/
1219: 	}
1220: 	cpu_profileReset();
1221: }
1222: 
1223: void cpu_exec(CPU_t* cpu, uint32_t execloops) {
1224: 
1225: 	uint32_t loopcount;
1226: 	uint8_t docontinue;
1227: 	static uint16_t firstip;
1228: 	static uint16_t last_ip = 0;
1229: 	static uint8_t ip_repeat_count = 0;
1230: 	static uint64_t last_exec_log = 0;
1231: 	static uint8_t diag_due = 0;
1232: 
1233: 	/* Hot-address sampler is driven from inside the instruction loop below. */
1234: 
1235: 	/*
1236: 		Both diagnostics below write to /sdcard, which is FUSE-backed on the
1237: 		target and costs 8-10ms per flush, so they have to stay rare. Rate-limit
1238: 		them on retired instructions (cpu->totalexec), not on calls into this
1239: 		function: execloops is typically 10000, so counting calls made the
1240: 		interval 10000x larger than intended.
1241: 	*/
1242: 	if (cpu->ip == last_ip) {
1243: 		ip_repeat_count++;
1244: 		static uint16_t last_cx = 0;
1245: 		if (ip_repeat_count == 200) {
1246: 			if ((cpu->regs.wordregs[regcx] == last_cx) && diag_due) {
1247: 				DIAG("CPU STUCK: IP=0x%04X CS=0x%04X repeating, CX not changing, AX=%04X BX=%04X CX=%04X DX=%04X SI=%04X DI=%04X",
1248: 					cpu->ip, cpu->segregs[regcs], cpu->regs.wordregs[regax], cpu->regs.wordregs[regbx],
1249: 					cpu->regs.wordregs[regcx], cpu->regs.wordregs[regdx], cpu->regs.wordregs[regsi],
1250: 					cpu->regs.wordregs[regdi]);
1251: 				diag_due = 0;
1252: 			}
1253: 		}
1254: 		last_cx = cpu->regs.wordregs[regcx];
1255: 	} else {
1256: 		ip_repeat_count = 0;
1257: 	}
1258: 	last_ip = cpu->ip;
1259: 
1260: 	if (cpu->totalexec - last_exec_log >= CPU_DIAG_INTERVAL) {
1261: 		last_exec_log = cpu->totalexec;
1262: 		diag_due = 1;
1263: 		DIAG("CPU: exec_count=%llu IP=0x%04X CS=0x%04X AX=%04X BX=%04X CX=%04X DX=%04X SP=%04X BP=%04X SI=%04X DI=%04X",
1264: 			(unsigned long long)cpu->totalexec, cpu->ip, cpu->segregs[regcs],
1265: 			cpu->regs.wordregs[regax], cpu->regs.wordregs[regbx], cpu->regs.wordregs[regcx],
1266: 			cpu->regs.wordregs[regdx], cpu->regs.wordregs[regsp], cpu->regs.wordregs[regbp],
1267: 			cpu->regs.wordregs[regsi], cpu->regs.wordregs[regdi]);
1268: 	}
1269: 
1270: 	for (loopcount = 0; loopcount < execloops; loopcount++) {
1271: 
1272: 		/*
1273: 			Instruction-level hot-address sample. Once per 256 instructions is
1274: 			~0.4% overhead and gives an unbiased distribution; sampling only at
1275: 			the top of this function (once per 10000 instructions) just showed
1276: 			which interrupt handler the emulator happened to be inside.
1277: 		*/
1278: 		if (trace_flags & TRACE_FLAG_CPU && (loopcount & 0xFF) == 0) {
1279: 			cpu_profile_add(((uint32_t)cpu->segregs[regcs] << 4) + (uint32_t)cpu->ip);
1280: 		}
1281: 
1282: 		if (cpu->trap_toggle) {
1283: 			cpu_intcall(cpu, 1);
1284: 		}
1285: 
1286: 		if (cpu->tf) {
1287: 			cpu->trap_toggle = 1;
1288: 		}
1289: 		else {
1290: 			cpu->trap_toggle = 0;
1291: 		}
1292: 
1293: 		if (cpu->hltstate) goto skipexecution;
1294: 
1295: 		cpu->reptype = 0;
1296: 		cpu->segoverride = 0;
1297: 		cpu->useseg = cpu->segregs[regds];
1298: 		docontinue = 0;
1299: 		firstip = cpu->ip;
1300: 
1301: 		while (!docontinue) {
1302: 			cpu->segregs[regcs] = cpu->segregs[regcs] & 0xFFFF;
1303: 			cpu->ip = cpu->ip & 0xFFFF;
1304: 			cpu->savecs = cpu->segregs[regcs];
1305: 			cpu->saveip = cpu->ip;
1306: 			// __android_log_print(ANDROID_LOG_ERROR, "XTulator-CPU", "cpu_exec: fetching opcode at CS=%04X IP=%04X (phys=%05X)", cpu->segregs[regcs], cpu->ip, (cpu->segregs[regcs] << 4) + cpu->ip);
1307: 			cpu->opcode = getmem8(cpu, cpu->segregs[regcs], cpu->ip);
1308: 			StepIP(cpu, 1);

1310: 			switch (cpu->opcode) {

1317: 			case 0x3E:	/* segment cpu->segregs[regds] */

1319: 				cpu->segoverride = 1;

1322: 			case 0x26:	/* segment cpu->segregs[reges] */

1327: 			case 0x36:	/* segment cpu->segregs[regss] */

1337: 			case 0xF2:	/* REPNE/REPNZ */

1347: 		cpu->totalexec++;

1374: 		case 0x3:	/* 03 ADD Gv Ev */

1377: 			cpu->oper2 = readrm16(cpu, cpu->rm);

38: uint8_t i8259_read(I8259_t* i8259, uint16_t portnum) {
39: #ifdef DEBUG_PIC

56: void i8259_write(I8259_t* i8259, uint16_t portnum, uint8_t value) {
57: #ifdef DEBUG_PIC
58: 	debug_log(DEBUG_DETAIL, "[I8259] Write port 0x%X: %X\n", portnum, value);
59: #endif

61: 	case 0:
62: 		if (value & 0x10) { //ICW1

68: 			i8259->icwstep = 2;

70: 		}

72: #ifdef DEBUG_PIC

74: #endif
75: 			i8259->ocw[2] = value;
76: 			switch (value & 0xE0) {
77: 			case 0x60: //specific EOI
78: 				i8259->irr &= ~(1 << (value & 0x03));
79: 				i8259->isr &= ~(1 << (value & 0x03));
80: 				break;
81: 			case 0x40: //no operation
82: 				break;
83: 			case 0x20: //non-specific EOI
84: 				i8259->irr &= ~i8259->isr;
85: 				i8259->isr = 0x00;
86: 				break;
87: 			default: //other

89: 				debug_log(DEBUG_DETAIL, "[I8259] Unhandled EOI type: %u\r\n", value & 0xE0);

91: 				break;
92: 			}

95: #ifdef DEBUG_PIC

97: #endif
98: 			i8259->ocw[3] = value;
99: 			if (value & 0x02) {
100: 				i8259->readmode = value & 1;
101: 			}
102: 		}
103: 		break;

140: uint8_t i8259_nextintr(I8259_t* i8259) {
141: 	uint8_t i, tmpirr;
142: 	tmpirr = i8259->irr & (~i8259->imr); //AND request register with inverted mask register
143: 	for (i = 0; i < 8; i++)
144: 		if ((tmpirr >> i) & 1) {
145: 			i8259->irr &= ~(1 << i);
146: 			i8259->isr |= (1 << i);
147: 			I8259_LOGI("i8259_nextintr: CPU acknowledged IRQ %d, vector 0x%02X", i, i8259->icw[2] + i);
148: 			return(i8259->icw[2] + i);
149: 		}
150: 	return 0;
151: }
152: 
153: void i8259_doirq(I8259_t* i8259, uint8_t irqnum) {
154: 	I8259_LOGI("i8259_doirq: raising IRQ %d", irqnum);
155: #ifdef DEBUG_PIC
156: 	debug_log(DEBUG_DETAIL, "[I8259] IRQ %u raised\r\n", irqnum);
157: #endif
158: 	i8259->irr |= (1 << irqnum) & (~i8259->imr);
159: }

161: void i8259_init(I8259_t* i8259) {
162: 	memset(i8259, 0, sizeof(I8259_t));
163: 	i8259->intoffset = 8;

29: #define LOG_TAG "XTulator-JNI"
30: #define CPU_SPEED_REF_MHZ 4.77
31: /*
32: 	LOGI/LOGE/LOGW are gated on TRACE_FLAG_MISC so they only fire when
33: 	the "other" tracing category is explicitly enabled.  Keyboard-specific
34: 	logging uses LOGKEY (TRACE_FLAG_KEYBOARD) and per-iteration CPU sampling
35: 	uses LOGCPU (TRACE_FLAG_CPU), keeping the hot path logd-free by default.
36: */
37: #define LOGI(...) do { if (trace_flags & TRACE_FLAG_MISC) { __android_log_print(ANDROID_LOG_INFO, LOG_TAG, __VA_ARGS__); } } while (0)
38: #define LOGE(...) do { if (trace_flags & TRACE_FLAG_MISC) { __android_log_print(ANDROID_LOG_ERROR, LOG_TAG, __VA_ARGS__); } } while (0)
39: #define LOGW(...) do { if (trace_flags & TRACE_FLAG_MISC) { __android_log_print(ANDROID_LOG_WARN, LOG_TAG, __VA_ARGS__); } } while (0)
40: #define LOGKEY(...) do { if (trace_flags & TRACE_FLAG_KEYBOARD) { __android_log_print(ANDROID_LOG_INFO, "XTulator-KEY", __VA_ARGS__); } } while (0)
41: #define LOGCPU(...) do { if (trace_flags & TRACE_FLAG_CPU) { __android_log_print(ANDROID_LOG_ERROR, LOG_TAG, __VA_ARGS__); } } while (0)

58: /* Ring buffer for key scancodes (press=0x00-0x7F, release=0x80-0xFF).
59:  * Size must be power of 2 for fast modulo. */
60: #define KEYBUF_SIZE 16

65: static void optimer(void* dummy) {
66: 	/*
67: 		optimer runs at 10Hz and ops is reset every tick, so ops holds the
68: 		instructions retired in the last 0.1s. Multiply by 10 for a per-second
69: 		rate. Reported through DIAG rather than logcat so it can be read off a
70: 		device with no debugger; DIAG block-buffers, so these lines appear in
71: 		batches rather than one per second.
72: 	*/
73: 	(void)dummy;
74: 	{
75: 		double mips = ((double)ops * 10.0) / 1000000.0;
76: 		cpu_speed_pct = (uint32_t)(mips / CPU_SPEED_REF_MHZ * 100.0 + 0.5);
77: 		if (showMIPS) {
78: 			debug_log(DEBUG_INFO, "%.3f MIPS (%u%%)\r", mips, (unsigned)cpu_speed_pct);
79: 		}
80: 	}
81: 	if ((trace_flags & TRACE_FLAG_MISC) && ++optimer_ticks >= 10) {
82: 		optimer_ticks = 0;
83: 		DIAG("PERF: %.3f MIPS (%llu instructions in the last 0.1s)",
84: 			((double)ops * 10.0) / 1000000.0, (unsigned long long)ops);
85: 		/* Read the hottest address before cpu_profileDump() resets the table. */
86: 		profile_watch = (int)cpu_hottest();
87: 		cpu_profileDump();
88: 		/* Dump the code around whatever the sampler just found hottest. */
89: 		if (profile_watch > 0 && profile_watch != 0xFFFFFFFF) {
90: 			cpu_dumpmem(&machine.CPU, (uint32_t)profile_watch, 48);
91: 		}
92: 		i8253_debugDump(timing_getCur() - pit_last_dump);
93: 		pit_last_dump = timing_getCur();
94: 		i8253_debugReset();
95: 	}
96: 	ops = 0;
97: }

102: }

104: void setspeed(double mhz) {
105: 	if (mhz > 0) {
106: 		speed = mhz;
107: 		instructionsperloop = (uint32_t)(speed * 1e6 / 140000.0);
108: 		limitCPU = 1;
109: 		timing_timerEnable(cpuLimitTimer);
110: 	} else {
111: 		speed = 0;
112: 		instructionsperloop = 100;
113: 		limitCPU = 0;
114: 		timing_timerDisable(cpuLimitTimer);
115: 	}
116: }

118: JNIEXPORT jint JNICALL Java_com_xtulator_android_XTulatorActivity_nativeInit(JNIEnv *env, jobject thiz, jstring biosPath, jstring diskPath) {
119: 	const char* biosPathStr;
120: 	const char* lastSlash;
121: 	size_t dlen;
122: 	char dirbuf[1024];
123: 	const char* diskPathStr;
124: 
125: 	(void)thiz;
126: 
127: 	LOGE("nativeInit: CALLED");
128: 	sprintf(title, "%s v%s", STR_TITLE, STR_VERSION);
129: 	LOGI("nativeInit: title=%s", title);
130: 	DIAG("nativeInit: starting");
131: 
132: 	if (biosPath != NULL) {
133: 		biosPathStr = (*env)->GetStringUTFChars(env, biosPath, NULL);
134: 		if (biosPathStr != NULL) {
135: 			lastSlash = strrchr(biosPathStr, '/');
136: 			if (lastSlash != NULL) {
137: 				dlen = (size_t)(lastSlash - biosPathStr);
138: 				if (dlen < sizeof(dirbuf)) {
139: 					memcpy(dirbuf, biosPathStr, dlen);
140: 					dirbuf[dlen] = '\0';
141: 					LOGI("nativeInit: chdir to %s", dirbuf);
142: 					int chdir_ret = chdir(dirbuf);
143: 					LOGI("nativeInit: chdir return value = %d", chdir_ret);
144: 					if (chdir_ret != 0) {
145: 						LOGI("nativeInit: chdir failed: %s", strerror(errno));
146: 						DIAG("nativeInit: chdir to '%s' FAILED: %s", dirbuf, strerror(errno));
147: 					} else {
148: 						DIAG("nativeInit: chdir to '%s' OK", dirbuf);
149: 					}
150: 
151: 				}
152: 			}
153: 			(*env)->ReleaseStringUTFChars(env, biosPath, biosPathStr);
154: 		}
155: 	}
156: 
157: 	LOGI("nativeInit: calling ports_init");
158: 	ports_init();
159: 	LOGI("nativeInit: calling timing_init");
160: 	timing_init();
161: 	LOGI("nativeInit: calling memory_init");
162: 	memory_init();
163: 	machine.pcap_if = -1;
164: 
165: 	if (diskPath != NULL) {
166: 		diskPathStr = (*env)->GetStringUTFChars(env, diskPath, NULL);
167: 		if (diskPathStr != NULL) {
168: 			LOGI("nativeInit: calling biosdisk_insert with %s", diskPathStr);
169: 			char diskPathCopy[1024];
170: 			strncpy(diskPathCopy, diskPathStr, sizeof(diskPathCopy) - 1);
171: 			diskPathCopy[sizeof(diskPathCopy) - 1] = '\0';
172: 			(*env)->ReleaseStringUTFChars(env, diskPath, diskPathStr);
173: 			diskPathStr = NULL;
174: 			biosdisk_insert(&machine.CPU, 0, diskPathCopy);
175: 		}
176: 	}
177: 
178: 	LOGI("nativeInit: calling sdlconsole_init");
179: 	if (sdlconsole_init(title) != 0) {
180: 		LOGI("nativeInit: sdlconsole_init failed");
181: 		return -1;
182: 	}
183: 	LOGI("nativeInit: sdlconsole_init OK");
184: 	if (sdlaudio_init(&machine) != 0) {
185: 		LOGI("nativeInit: sdlaudio_init failed");
186: 	}
187: 	LOGI("nativeInit: calling machine_init");
188: 	if (machine_init(&machine, usemachine) < 0) {
189: 		LOGI("nativeInit: machine_init failed");
190: 		return -1;
191: 	}
192: 	LOGI("nativeInit: machine_init OK");
193: 
194: 	if (bootdrive == 0xFF) {
195: 		bootdrive = biosdisk[0].inserted ? 0x00 : (biosdisk[2].inserted ? 0x80 : 0x00);
196: 	}
197: 
198: 	LOGI("nativeInit: adding timers");
199: 	timing_addTimer((void*)optimer, NULL, 10.0, TIMING_ENABLED);
200: 	cpuLimitTimer = timing_addTimer((void*)cputimer, NULL, 10000.0, TIMING_DISABLED);
201: 	if (speed > 0) {
202: 		setspeed(speed);
203: 	}
204: 
205: 	DIAG("nativeInit: completed successfully");
206: 	/*
207: 		This function is declared jint and the success path used to fall off the
208: 		end, so it returned whatever happened to be in the return register. The
209: 		Java side treats any non-zero as "Native init failed" and logs it, which
210: 		made a successful init look like a failure (observed: 1107444095).
211: 	*/
212: 	return 0;
213: }

215: JNIEXPORT void JNICALL Java_com_xtulator_android_XTulatorActivity_nativeRun(JNIEnv *env, jobject thiz) {
216: 	LOGE("nativeRun: ENTRY");
217: 	(void)env; (void)thiz;
218: 	LOGE("nativeRun: starting loop");
219: 
220: 	uint32_t loop_count = 0;
221: 	while (running) {
222: 		loop_count++;
223: 		if ((trace_flags & TRACE_FLAG_CPU) && loop_count % 1000 == 0) {
224: 			LOGCPU("nativeRun: loop %u, IP=%04X:%04X", loop_count, machine.CPU.segregs[regcs], machine.CPU.ip);
225: 		}
226: 		cpu_interruptCheck(&machine.CPU, &machine.i8259);
227: 		cpu_exec(&machine.CPU, instructionsperloop);
228: 		ops += instructionsperloop;
229: 
230: 		if (limitCPU && !goCPU) {
231: 			usleep(100);
232: 		}
233: 
234: 		timing_loop();
235: 
236: 	  /* Drain one scancode per iteration: the 8088 reads port 0x60 once per
237: 	   * IRQ1, so feeding a whole burst into KeyState at once would overwrite
238: 	   * the pending byte and drop every key except the last. */
239: 		if (keybuf_head != keybuf_tail) {
240: 			uint8_t sc = keybuf[keybuf_tail];
241: 			keybuf_tail = (keybuf_tail + 1) & (KEYBUF_SIZE - 1);
242: 			LOGKEY("Injecting scancode=0x%02X", sc);
243: 			machine.KeyState.scancode = sc;
244: 			machine.KeyState.isNew = 1;
245: 			i8259_doirq(&machine.i8259, 1);
246: 		}
247: 	}
248: 	LOGE("nativeRun: emulation stopped");
249: }
